recipes.title: Aubergine parmigiana
ingredients: 60 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C). Cut the aubergines into slices about 1 cm thick, brush both sides with 4 tbsp of the oil, spread over two baking trays and roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until soft and golden.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, sugar and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in most of the basil.

Turn the oven down to 190°C (fan 170°C). In a baking dish, layer a little sauce, then aubergine, mozzarella and a sprinkle of hard cheese. Repeat the layers, finishing with sauce and the remaining hard cheese.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top. Rest for 10 minutes, then scatter with the remaining basil and serve.

recipes.title: Baked cod with herb crumb
ingredients: 600 g skinless cod fillets, cut into four pieces
1 lemon, zested, then cut into wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of the salt on a baking tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the breadcrumbs, parsley, lemon zest, garlic, the remaining 2 tbsp oil and the rest of the salt and pepper in a mixing bowl until the crumbs look evenly moistened.
Pat the cod dry with kitchen paper and brush the tops thinly with the mustard. Press the herb crumb firmly onto the mustard-coated side of each piece.
Push the potatoes to the edges of the tray, sit the cod in the middle and bake for 12–15 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish is opaque and flakes easily (63°C in the thickest part).
While the fish bakes, cook the peas in a saucepan of boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Serve the cod with the potatoes, peas and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

recipes.title: Baked falafel with tahini sauce
ingredients: 480 g canned chickpeas, drained, rinsed and patted dry
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C) and brush a baking tray with 1 tbsp of the oil.

Put the chickpeas, onion, two of the garlic cloves, the herbs, cumin, ground coriander, chilli, gram flour, baking powder and most of the salt in a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped and the mixture holds together when pressed, but is not a smooth paste.
Shape into 16 small patties, place on the tray and brush the tops with the remaining oil. Bake for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp on both sides.
Meanwhile, cook the quinoa in a saucepan of boiling water for 12–15 minutes until tender, then drain.

For the sauce, crush the remaining garlic clove and whisk it with the tahini, half the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and the cold water in a small bowl. It will thicken at first, then loosen into a smooth, pourable sauce.
Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the remaining lemon juice and salt. Serve the falafel on the quinoa with the salad and drizzle with tahini sauce.

recipes.title: Beef and broccoli
ingredients: 550 g rump steak, trimmed and thinly sliced across the grain
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.

Toss the beef with the cornflour and 1 tbsp of the tamari in a mixing bowl. In a small jug, mix the remaining tamari, honey, sesame oil and 4 tbsp water. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw meat.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over a high heat with 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil. Stir-fry the beef in two batches for 1–2 minutes until browned, then tip onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the broccoli and 3 tbsp water. Cover and steam-fry for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender. Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss for 1–2 minutes until glossy and the beef is cooked to at least 63°C.
Serve over the rice, topped with spring onions if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Beef bibimbap bowls
ingredients: 2 tbsp gochujang, loosened with a little water
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan according to the packet instructions; keep covered and warm. Mix the soy sauce, sugar, 1 tsp of the sesame oil and the garlic in a small bowl.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Fry the beef for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining (71°C). Add the soy mixture and cook for 1 minute until sticky. Tip into a bowl and keep warm.

Wipe the pan, add another 1 tbsp oil and stir-fry the carrots and courgette separately for 2–3 minutes each until just tender. Wilt the spinach and beansprouts in the pan for 1–2 minutes, then toss with the salt and remaining sesame oil.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the eggs until the whites are fully set and the edges are crisp.
Divide the rice between four bowls. Arrange the beef and vegetables in sections on top, add a fried egg to each and serve with the gochujang and sesame seeds for everyone to mix in.

recipes.title: Homemade beef burgers
ingredients: 600 g beef mince, not extra lean
steps: Mix the mince, onion, salt, pepper and garlic granules in a mixing bowl with your hands, without overworking. Shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick, pressing a slight dip into the centre of each. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Chill the patties for 10 minutes if you have time; it helps them hold their shape.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or griddle over a medium-high heat. Cook the burgers for 5–6 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through to 71°C with no pink remaining.
Add the cheese slices for the last minute if using, and cover the pan so they melt.
Meanwhile, toast the cut sides of the buns under the grill or in a dry pan.
Build the burgers with lettuce, tomato and ketchup if using. Serve with oven chips or corn on the cob.

recipes.title: Beef koftas with yogurt sauce
ingredients: 1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
8 skewers, soaked in water if wooden, optional
steps: Mix the mince, onion, half the garlic, the spices, parsley and salt in a mixing bowl. Divide into 8 portions and shape each into a long sausage shape, threading onto skewers if using. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Stir the yogurt, cucumber, mint, lemon juice and remaining garlic together with a pinch of salt to make the sauce. Chill until needed.
Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.

Heat the grill to high or heat a griddle pan over a medium-high heat. Brush the koftas with oil and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred and cooked through to 71°C with no pink remaining.
Serve the koftas on the rice with the yogurt sauce and a chopped tomato and cucumber salad. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Beef lasagne
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes until soft. Add the mince and brown for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.

Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, oregano, 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Simmer for 25 minutes until thick. The mince should reach 71°C with no pink remaining.

Meanwhile, make the white sauce: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Keep whisking over a medium heat for 5 minutes until thick, then season with the nutmeg and remaining salt.

Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a large baking dish, then layer lasagne sheets, meat sauce and white sauce, repeating to make three layers and finishing with white sauce.
Scatter over the mozzarella and Parmesan and bake for 40–45 minutes until bubbling and golden and a knife slides easily through the pasta.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting. Lasagne freezes well whole or in portions; reheat until piping hot in the centre.

recipes.title: Beef stew with carrots and potatoes
ingredients: 700 g braising steak, cut into chunks
600 g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C). Toss the beef with the cornflour, salt and pepper in a mixing bowl. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw meat.
Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish over a medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for 4–5 minutes each, then lift onto a plate.
Lower the heat, add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute, then pour in the stock, scraping up the browned bits from the base.
Return the beef with the thyme and bay leaves, bring to a simmer, cover and transfer to the oven for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Stir in the carrots and potatoes, cover and return to the oven for another 50–60 minutes until the beef is very tender and the vegetables are cooked through. The beef will be well above 63°C.
Remove the herb stalks and bay leaves, check the seasoning and scatter with parsley if using. The stew keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Beef stroganoff
ingredients: 550 g sirloin or rump steak, trimmed and cut into thin strips
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.

Season the beef with half the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and sear the beef in two batches for 1–2 minutes until browned but still pink inside. Tip onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw meat.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and the butter, then the onion. Cook for 5 minutes, add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes more until golden.
Stir in the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then pour in the stock and bubble for 3–4 minutes until reduced by about a third.
Lower the heat and stir in the soured cream and remaining salt. Return the beef and any juices and warm through gently for 2 minutes without boiling, until the beef reaches at least 63°C.
Serve over the rice, scattered with parsley if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Black bean burgers
ingredients: 480 g canned black beans, drained, rinsed and patted dry
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute. Tip into a mixing bowl.
Add the beans to the bowl and mash with a potato masher or fork until mostly smooth with some whole beans left.
Stir in the sweetcorn, breadcrumbs, flour and salt until the mixture holds together when squeezed. Shape into four patties about 2 cm thick and chill for 15 minutes if you have time, to firm up.
Wipe the frying pan, heat the remaining oil over medium heat and cook the burgers for 4–5 minutes per side, turning carefully, until crisp and hot all the way through.
Toast the buns lightly, then fill with lettuce, tomato, a burger and avocado, if using.

recipes.title: Butter chicken
ingredients: 650 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
steps: Mix the yogurt, half the salt, half the garam masala, the cumin, chilli powder and turmeric in a mixing bowl. Add the chicken, stir to coat and leave for 15 minutes. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken in batches for 4–5 minutes. Lift onto a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan, add the onion and cook gently for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the passata, sugar, remaining garam masala and remaining salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, then blend with a stick blender until smooth.
Return the chicken to the sauce, stir in the cream and simmer gently for 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 74°C with juices running clear.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes, then drain. Serve the curry with the rice. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Chicken and broccoli pasta bake
ingredients: 250 g broccoli, cut into small florets
500 g chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, adding the broccoli for the final 2 minutes. Drain.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6–8 minutes until golden and cooked through to 74°C with no pink remaining. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and keep whisking for 4–5 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Take the sauce off the heat and stir in the mustard, two-thirds of the cheese, the salt and pepper.
Mix the pasta, broccoli, chicken and sauce together and tip into a large baking dish. Scatter over the remaining cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Chicken burrito bowls
ingredients: 240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Mix half the oil with the paprika, cumin, chilli powder and half the salt in a mixing bowl and rub over the chicken. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender. Drain, then stir in the zest and juice of one lime and the remaining salt.

Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until well browned and the thickest part reaches 74°C with juices running clear. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Meanwhile, warm the black beans and sweetcorn together in a small saucepan for 3–4 minutes.
Mix the tomatoes and red onion with the juice of half the remaining lime to make a quick salsa. Cut the rest of the lime into wedges.

Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chicken, beans and sweetcorn, salsa and avocado. Scatter with coriander if using and serve with lime wedges. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Chicken cacciatore
steps: Season the chicken with half the salt and the pepper. Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan or casserole over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 3–4 minutes per side. Lift onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion, pepper and mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock, rosemary, oregano and remaining salt. Bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid, add the olives and simmer for 5 more minutes to thicken the sauce. The chicken should reach 74°C at the thickest part with juices running clear.
Discard the rosemary stalks, scatter with parsley if using and serve with mashed potatoes, rice or crusty bread. This freezes well for up to 3 months; cool quickly and reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Chicken enchiladas
ingredients: 240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and soften the onion and pepper for 6 minutes.

Add the chicken and cook for 6–8 minutes until it reaches 74°C with no pink remaining. Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Stir in the black beans, 4 tbsp of the passata and half the salt, then take off the heat.
In a small saucepan, warm the remaining passata with the oregano and remaining salt for 5 minutes to make the sauce. Spread a third of it over the base of a large baking dish.
Divide the chicken filling between the tortillas, roll them up and lay them seam side down in the dish. Pour over the rest of the sauce and scatter with the cheese.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden. Scatter with coriander if using. Assembled enchiladas can be frozen before baking; defrost in the fridge and bake until piping hot.

recipes.title: Chicken fajitas
steps: Mix the paprika, cumin, chilli powder, garlic granules and salt in a mixing bowl. Add the sliced chicken and half the oil and toss to coat. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the peppers and onion and stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until softened and slightly charred, then tip onto a plate.
Add the chicken to the hot pan in a single layer and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and cooked through to 74°C with no pink remaining.
Return the vegetables to the pan, squeeze over the lime juice and toss together for a minute.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan or the microwave for a few seconds each.
Serve the filling at the table with the warm tortillas so everyone can fill and roll their own, with soured cream, avocado and coriander if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken katsu curry
steps: For the sauce, heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan over a medium heat and cook the onion and carrots for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook for 1 minute.

Pour in the stock, honey and soy sauce and simmer for 15 minutes until the carrots are very tender. Blend until smooth with a stick blender, then mix the cornflour with a little water, stir it in and simmer for 2 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Place each chicken breast between sheets of cling film and bash with a rolling pin to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with the salt.
Set up three shallow bowls with the flour, beaten eggs and panko. Dip each breast in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing to coat. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a baking tray and bake for 10–12 minutes until the centre reaches 74°C and juices run clear.
While the chicken cooks, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the chicken with a sharp knife and serve on the rice with the curry sauce poured alongside. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Chicken pot pie
ingredients: 600 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Lift onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the onion, carrots and celery and cook over a medium heat for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock and milk, stirring until smooth. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thickened.
Return the chicken with the peas, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes. Spoon into a pie dish.
Unroll the pastry and lay it over the dish, trimming the edges and pressing them onto the rim. Cut a small slit in the middle and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden and the filling is bubbling. Check the filling has reached 74°C. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken and prawn paella
ingredients: 500 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat the oil in a paella pan or large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 5 minutes, turning, then lift onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.

Crumble the saffron into the stock. Add the rice to the pan and stir to coat, then add the tomatoes, stock, salt and the chicken. Stir once, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered without stirring for 18 minutes.

Scatter the prawns and peas over the top, pressing them in lightly. Cook for 5–7 minutes more, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid, the prawns are pink and opaque throughout and the chicken reaches 74°C with juices running clear.
Take off the heat, cover with a clean tea towel or foil and rest for 5 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Chicken shawarma bowls
steps: Mix the oil, half the lemon juice, the spices, two-thirds of the garlic and the salt in a mixing bowl. Add the chicken and coat well; leave for 15 minutes or up to a day in the fridge. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C). Spread the chicken on a baking tray and roast for 20–25 minutes until charred at the edges and the thickest part reaches 74°C with juices running clear.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the remaining garlic and lemon juice into the yogurt with a pinch of salt to make a garlic sauce.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice it with a sharp knife.

Divide the rice between bowls and top with the chicken, cucumber, tomatoes and red onion. Spoon over the garlic sauce and scatter with parsley if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Chicken and sweet potato traybake
ingredients: 800 g sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
2 red peppers, deseeded and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (fan 190°C). Mix the oil, paprika, cumin, garlic granules, salt and pepper in a large mixing bowl.
Toss the sweet potatoes, onions and peppers in half the spiced oil and spread over a large baking tray. Roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the chicken to the bowl with the remaining spiced oil and turn to coat. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Nestle the chicken among the vegetables and roast for 25 minutes more, turning the vegetables once, until the sweet potatoes are tender and caramelised at the edges.
Check the chicken reaches 74°C at the thickest part with juices running clear. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing over if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken tikka masala
ingredients: 650 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks
steps: Mix the yogurt with half the garam masala, half the cumin, half the paprika, the turmeric and half the salt in a mixing bowl. Stir in the chicken and leave for at least 15 minutes (or up to a day in the fridge). Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the chicken on a lined baking tray and grill for 10–12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. It will finish cooking in the sauce.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, chilli powder and the remaining spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Blitz with a stick blender until smooth if you like.
Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the cream and grilled chicken into the sauce and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the chicken reaches 74°C and the juices run clear.
Serve the curry over the rice, scattered with coriander if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Chilli con carne
ingredients: 240 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over a medium heat and cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until softened.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and brown for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Stir in the garlic, chilli powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, kidney beans, stock and salt. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 30–35 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich. The mince should reach 71°C with no pink remaining.
About 15 minutes before the end, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the chilli over the rice, scattered with coriander if using. Freeze leftover chilli in portions for up to 3 months; cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Cod in tomato and olive sauce
ingredients: 600 g skinless cod fillets, cut into four pieces
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water according to the packet instructions, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato purée, oregano, sugar, olives and capers. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened, then season with the salt and pepper.
Nestle the cod into the sauce and spoon some sauce over the top. Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (63°C).
Scatter with parsley and serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Cottage pie
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and cook the onion, carrots and celery for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince. Stir in the tomato purée and cornflour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, add the thyme and half the salt and the pepper, and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas and check the mince has reached 71°C with no pink remaining.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender, drain well and mash with the butter, milk and remaining salt.
Spoon the mince into a baking dish, top with the mash and rough up the surface with a fork. Scatter with Cheddar if using.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges. The assembled pie can be frozen before baking; defrost in the fridge and bake until piping hot in the centre.

recipes.title: Fish pie
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
450 g fish pie mix, skinless cod, salmon and smoked haddock
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender, then drain and mash with 50 g of the butter and 100 ml of the milk. Season with half the salt.

Meanwhile, melt the remaining 40 g butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the remaining 500 ml milk, add the bay leaf and simmer, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until smooth and thick. Remove the bay leaf and season with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Spread the raw fish, prawns and peas over the base of a baking dish of about 2 litres. Stir the parsley into the sauce and pour it over evenly.
Spoon the mash over the top, starting at the edges to seal, then rough it up with a fork and scatter over the cheese.

Set the dish on a baking tray and bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges, the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the prawns are pink throughout. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
To batch cook, cool the assembled unbaked pie, cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, then bake for 45–50 minutes until piping hot in the centre.

recipes.title: Fish tacos with lime slaw
ingredients: 600 g skinless white fish fillets, such as cod or haddock
15 g fresh coriander, leaves picked, optional
steps: Make the slaw: zest one lime and juice both. In a mixing bowl, toss the cabbage and carrot with the mayonnaise, half the lime juice and a pinch of the salt. Set aside while you cook the fish.
Pat the fish dry and cut into large chunks, about 4 cm. Mix the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, lime zest and remaining salt, then rub over the fish.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fish for 2–3 minutes per side, turning carefully, until opaque all the way through and it flakes easily (63°C). Squeeze over the remaining lime juice.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for about 30 seconds each side, or wrap in foil and warm in a low oven for 5 minutes.
Fill each tortilla with slaw and a few chunks of fish, and top with avocado and coriander if you like.

recipes.title: Garlic prawn linguine
steps: Cook the linguine in a large pot of well-salted boiling water according to the packet instructions. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and chilli and cook gently for 2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and just pale gold, not brown.
Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until they start to soften. Add the prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until pink and opaque throughout.
Add the drained linguine, lemon zest and juice, parsley and salt, and toss well, adding splashes of the pasta water until the pasta is glossy and coated. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Gnocchi with tomato and mozzarella
ingredients: 30 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
15 g fresh basil, leaves torn, optional
steps: Heat the oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, sugar and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the gnocchi in a large pot of boiling water according to the packet instructions, until they float to the surface. Drain.
Heat the grill to high. Stir the gnocchi and spinach into the sauce until the spinach wilts. Scatter over the mozzarella and hard cheese.
Grill for 4–5 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden in spots. Scatter with basil, if using, and serve.

recipes.title: Greek chicken souvlaki
ingredients: 650 g chicken breasts, cut into chunks
8 skewers, soaked in water if wooden
1 tbsp fresh mint or dill, chopped
steps: Mix the oil, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, two-thirds of the garlic, the oregano, salt and pepper in a mixing bowl. Add the chicken, toss and leave for 15 minutes (or up to a day in the fridge). Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
For the tzatziki, stir the yogurt, cucumber, herbs, remaining garlic and remaining lemon juice together with a pinch of salt.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers. Heat the grill to high or heat a griddle pan over a medium-high heat.
Cook the skewers for 10–12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 74°C with no pink remaining.
Warm the pittas under the grill for a minute. Serve the chicken in or alongside the pittas with the tomatoes, red onion and tzatziki.

recipes.title: Halloumi and vegetable traybake
ingredients: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Put the potatoes on a large baking tray and roast with 1 tbsp of the oil for 15 minutes.
Add the peppers, courgettes, onion and chickpeas to the tray. Mix the remaining oil with the oregano, paprika, garlic and salt, pour over and toss everything together.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are softening and starting to char at the edges.
Add the tomatoes and lay the halloumi slices on top. Drizzle the halloumi with the honey and roast for 10–12 minutes more, until the halloumi is golden and the potatoes are tender.
Squeeze over some lemon and serve straight from the tray with the remaining wedges.

recipes.title: Honey garlic chicken drumsticks
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Line a baking tray with foil or baking paper.

Whisk the honey, tamari, garlic, rice vinegar, oil and pepper in a mixing bowl. Add the drumsticks and turn to coat, then arrange them on the tray. Keep the leftover sauce in the bowl. Wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Bake for 20 minutes, then turn the drumsticks and brush with a little of the reserved sauce.
Bake for another 20–25 minutes until sticky and dark golden and the thickest part reaches 74°C with juices running clear.
Meanwhile, pour the rest of the sauce into a small saucepan. Mix the cornflour with a tablespoon of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1–2 minutes until glossy and thickened.
Toss the cooked drumsticks in the glaze and sprinkle with sesame seeds and spring onions if using. Serve with rice or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Honey mustard salmon traybake
ingredients: 1 lemon, half juiced, half cut into wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the potatoes and onion with the oil and salt on a large baking tray and roast for 20 minutes, until starting to colour.
Meanwhile, mix the honey, both mustards, garlic and lemon juice in a small bowl.
Add the broccoli to the tray and turn it in the oil. Make spaces between the vegetables and lay in the salmon fillets. Spoon the honey mustard over the salmon.
Roast for 12–15 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily (63°C in the thickest part) and the potatoes are tender.
Serve with the lemon wedges and any glaze spooned from the tray.

ingredientsStructured.name: lemon
ingredientsStructured.note: half juiced, half cut into wedges

recipes.title: Jacket potatoes with beans and cheese
ingredients: 820 g canned gluten-free baked beans in tomato sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Prick the potatoes all over with a fork, rub with the oil and salt, and put them straight onto the oven shelf with a baking tray on the shelf below.
Bake for 1 hour–1 hour 15 minutes, until the skins are crisp and a knife slides easily into the centre.
Towards the end, warm the beans in a saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until bubbling and hot through.
Cut a cross in the top of each potato and squeeze the base to open it up. Add a little butter, if using, then spoon over the beans and top with the cheese.
Leftover baked potatoes can be cooled, refrigerated and reheated until piping hot within 2 days.

ingredientsStructured.name: canned gluten-free baked beans in tomato sauce

recipes.title: Chicken and sausage jambalaya
ingredients: 450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan or casserole over a medium-high heat. Fry the chorizo for 2–3 minutes until it releases its oil, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until browned. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook for 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, paprika, thyme and cayenne for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir to coat it in the spicy oil, then pour in the tomatoes, stock and salt. Bring to the boil.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid. The chicken should reach 74°C with no pink remaining.
Leave to stand off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes, then scatter with spring onions if using. Cool leftovers within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Lamb and chickpea tagine
ingredients: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole or heavy pot over a medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in two batches for 4–5 minutes each, then lift onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw meat.
Lower the heat, add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, ginger and spices and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock, honey and salt, then return the lamb. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the chickpeas and apricots and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce has thickened. The lamb will be well above 63°C.
Check the seasoning and scatter with coriander if using. Serve with rice or roasted vegetables. The tagine keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Lemon herb roast chicken thighs
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Zest the lemon into a large mixing bowl, then squeeze in the juice and add the olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Add the chicken thighs and halved potatoes to the bowl and toss until everything is well coated. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.

Tip everything into a large roasting tin or baking tray, arranging the chicken skin side up in a single layer with the potatoes around it. Tuck in the garlic, thyme, rosemary and the squeezed lemon halves.
Roast for 40–45 minutes, turning the potatoes once halfway, until the skin is golden and crisp and the potatoes are tender.
Check the chicken is cooked: the thickest part should reach 74°C and the juices should run clear. Return to the oven for a few more minutes if needed.
Spoon the pan juices over the chicken, scatter with parsley if using and serve straight from the tray.

recipes.title: Macaroni cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Cook the macaroni in a large pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, then drain.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Take the sauce off the heat and stir in the mustard, nutmeg, salt, pepper and three-quarters of the cheese until melted.
Stir the macaroni into the sauce and tip into a baking dish. Top with the cherry tomatoes, if using, then scatter over the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Moussaka
ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Cut the aubergines into slices about 1 cm thick. Brush the aubergine and potato slices with 3 tbsp of the oil, spread over two baking trays and roast for 20–25 minutes until tender.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, then add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon and oregano for 1 minute. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Stir in the tomato purée, tomatoes, water and half the salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick, and check the mince is cooked through with no pink remaining (71°C).

Make the topping: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer, stirring, for 4 minutes until thick. Off the heat, season with the nutmeg and remaining salt, cool for 5 minutes, then whisk in the egg and half the cheese.

Turn the oven down to 180°C (fan 160°C). Layer the potatoes in a baking dish, then half the aubergine, all the lamb sauce, and the remaining aubergine. Pour over the topping and scatter with the rest of the cheese.

Bake for 40–45 minutes, until deep golden and the topping is set in the centre. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting. Leftovers keep for 3 days in the fridge or freeze in portions; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Mushroom risotto
ingredients: 40 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 10 minutes. Lift them out, chop finely, and pour the soaking liquid into a saucepan with the stock, leaving any grit behind. Keep the stock warm over a low heat.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chestnut mushrooms for 6–8 minutes until golden and their liquid has evaporated. Lift out half for topping.
Lower the heat, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, thyme and porcini for 1 minute, then stir in the rice for 2 minutes until glossy.

Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and letting each ladle be nearly absorbed before adding the next, for 18–20 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite and the risotto is loose and creamy.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter, the cheese, salt and pepper. Cover and rest for 2 minutes, then serve topped with the reserved mushrooms and parsley.

recipes.title: Pan-fried trout with new potatoes
ingredients: 750 g new potatoes, halved if large
1 lemon, half juiced, half cut into wedges
2 tbsp fresh dill or parsley, chopped
steps: Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender, adding the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Drain and keep warm.
Pat the trout dry with kitchen paper and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Lay the trout in skin-side down and press gently for a few seconds so it stays flat. Cook for 3–4 minutes until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook for 1–2 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily (63°C). Lift onto warm plates.
Turn the heat down, add the butter to the pan and let it foam. Stir in the lemon juice, herbs and capers, if using, then toss in the potatoes and beans to coat.
Serve the trout with the buttery potatoes and beans and the lemon wedges.
