recipes.title: Paprika chicken with peppers
ingredients: 650 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into large chunks
3 mixed bell peppers, deseeded and sliced
steps: Season the chicken with half the salt. Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, turning. Lift onto a plate. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.

Add the onion and peppers to the pan and cook over a medium heat for 8–10 minutes until soft and sweet. Stir in the garlic, both paprikas and the tomato purée and cook for 1 minute, stirring so the paprika doesn't burn.

Pour in the tomatoes and stock, add the remaining salt and the pepper, then return the chicken. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the chicken reaches 74°C with juices running clear.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the chicken and peppers over the rice, scattered with parsley if using. Cool any leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Penne arrabbiata
ingredients: 15 g fresh parsley or basil, chopped, optional
steps: Warm the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and chilli and cook gently for 2 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and just turning golden.
Stir in the tomato purée for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich. Use less chilli for a milder sauce.
Meanwhile, cook the penne in a large pot of salted boiling water according to the packet instructions. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the penne into the sauce with a splash of the cooking water until glossy and well coated.
Serve scattered with the herbs, if using.

recipes.title: Pesto pasta with green beans and potatoes
ingredients: 40 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
300 g small waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into small chunks
200 g green beans, trimmed and halved
steps: Make the pesto: lightly toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until golden. Blitz in a blender or food processor with the basil, garlic, cheese, lemon juice and a pinch of the salt, then gradually blend in the oil until you have a loose paste.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the remaining salt. Add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the pasta to the same pot and cook according to the packet instructions, adding the green beans for the last 5 minutes. Everything should be tender at the same time.
Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain. Return the pasta, potatoes and beans to the pot off the heat.
Stir in the pesto with a few splashes of the cooking water until the sauce is creamy and coats everything. Serve straight away.

ingredientsStructured.name: small waxy potatoes
ingredientsStructured.note: peeled and cut into small chunks

recipes.title: Pork chops with apples
ingredients: 700 g new potatoes, halved if large
2 eating apples, cored and cut into wedges
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan of salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 15–18 minutes until tender. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain.

Meanwhile, season the pork chops with half the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the chops for 4–5 minutes per side until golden and they reach at least 63°C in the centre. Rest on a plate for 3 minutes. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw pork.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and fry the apples and onion over a medium heat for 6–8 minutes until golden and softened. Add the thyme leaves.

Mix the cornflour with a splash of the apple juice, then pour all the apple juice, stock and cornflour mix into the pan. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened, then season with the remaining salt.
Return the chops and any resting juices to the pan to warm through, and serve with the apples, sauce, potatoes and green beans.

recipes.title: Pork schnitzel
ingredients: 750 g new potatoes, halved if large
4 boneless pork loin steaks, fat trimmed
steps: Boil the potatoes in a large pot of salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain and toss with the butter and parsley; keep warm.
Meanwhile, lay each pork steak between two sheets of baking paper and bash with a rolling pin until about 5 mm thick.

Set out three shallow dishes: the flour mixed with the salt and pepper, the eggs beaten, and the breadcrumbs. Coat each steak in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to stick. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw pork.

Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry two schnitzels for 2–3 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through (at least 63°C in the centre). Drain on kitchen paper and repeat with the remaining oil and pork.
Rest the schnitzels for 3 minutes, then serve with the potatoes and lemon wedges for squeezing.

recipes.title: Pork and vegetable noodles
ingredients: 150 g mangetout or sugar snap peas
steps: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet, then drain and rinse in cold water so they don't stick.
Mix the tamari, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl to make the sauce.

Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add the pork mince and stir-fry for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 71°C with no pink remaining. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Add the garlic, ginger, pepper, carrots and mangetout and stir-fry for 3 minutes until just tender but still crunchy.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes until everything is coated and hot. Scatter with the spring onions and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Prawn pad thai
ingredients: 1 lime, half juiced, half cut into wedges
4 spring onions, cut into short lengths
40 g roasted unsalted peanuts, roughly chopped
15 g fresh coriander, leaves picked, optional
steps: Soak or cook the noodles according to the packet instructions until just pliable, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Mix the fish sauce, tamarind, sugar and lime juice in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque throughout. Push to one side.
Pour the eggs into the empty side of the wok and scramble for about 1 minute until set, then break up and mix with the prawns.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes until the noodles are hot and coated. Add the beansprouts and spring onions and toss for 1 minute more.
Serve topped with the peanuts, chilli flakes and coriander, if using, with lime wedges on the side.

ingredientsStructured.name: lime
ingredientsStructured.note: half juiced, half cut into wedges

recipes.title: Prawn and pea risotto
steps: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a saucepan and keep it warm over a low heat.

Heat the oil and half the butter in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the rice for 2 minutes until the grains look glossy.

Pour in the wine and let it bubble until almost absorbed. Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is nearly absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18–20 minutes.
When the rice is almost tender, stir in the prawns and peas with a final ladle of stock. Cook for 3–4 minutes, until the prawns are pink and opaque throughout.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the remaining butter, the Parmesan, lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon juice. Cover and rest for 2 minutes, then serve scattered with parsley.

recipes.title: Red lentil dal
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and, when they sizzle, add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander and chilli powder for 1 minute.

Add the lentils, tomatoes and water. Bring to the boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils have broken down and the dal is thick. Add a splash more water if it catches.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook in a separate saucepan according to the packet instructions.
Stir the coconut milk, salt and spinach into the dal and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Add the lemon juice and serve with the rice and coriander.
Dal keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes well; loosen with water when reheating until steaming hot. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Saag paneer
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook in a saucepan according to the packet instructions and keep warm.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the paneer for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift onto a plate.

Add the remaining oil and the cumin seeds to the pan. When they sizzle, add the onion and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the coriander, turmeric and garam masala for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thick. Add the spinach a handful at a time, stirring until wilted. For a smoother sauce, blitz briefly with a stick blender.
Stir in the cream, salt and paneer and simmer for 3–4 minutes until the paneer is hot through. Serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Sesame salmon with greens and rice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan according to the packet instructions.
Mix 2 tbsp of the tamari with the honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger. Put the salmon in a lined baking dish, spoon over the glaze and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily (63°C in the thickest part).

Meanwhile, heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the broccoli for 3 minutes, add the pak choi and a splash of water, and cook for 2 minutes more until just tender. Toss with the remaining tamari.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the greens, spooning over any juices from the dish, and scatter with spring onions, if using.

recipes.title: Slow cooker pulled pork
ingredients: 1.5 kg boneless pork shoulder, rind and excess fat removed
steps: Mix the sugar, paprika, cumin, garlic granules, salt and pepper in a small mixing bowl and rub all over the pork. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw pork.
Scatter the onion over the base of the slow cooker and sit the pork on top.
Whisk the passata, tomato purée, cider vinegar and honey together and pour over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours (or high for 5 hours) until the pork is very tender and falls apart easily. It will be well above 63°C.
Lift the pork onto a board and shred it with two forks, discarding any fat. Skim the fat from the sauce, then stir the shredded meat back into the slow cooker.
Pile into the buns with coleslaw if using. Cool leftovers within 2 hours and freeze in portions with some sauce for up to 3 months; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Spaghetti bolognese
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Stir in the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rich and thick. The mince should reach 71°C with no pink remaining.
About 12 minutes before the sauce is ready, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water according to the packet, then drain, reserving a splash of the cooking water.
Remove the bay leaf, toss the spaghetti with the sauce and a little pasta water, and serve with Parmesan if using. The sauce freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Spaghetti carbonara
ingredients: 60 g Parmesan or Pecorino, finely grated, plus extra to serve
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti according to the packet instructions.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the pancetta for 6–8 minutes until crisp, golden and cooked through. Take the pan off the heat.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs, egg yolks, cheese and pepper together until smooth.

Scoop out a mugful of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and tip it straight into the pancetta pan, still off the heat. Toss well so the pasta is coated in the fat and cools slightly for about 1 minute.

Pour in the egg mixture with a splash of pasta water and toss quickly and continuously. The heat of the pasta cooks the eggs: keep tossing for 2–3 minutes, adding more pasta water as needed, until the sauce has thickened and is glossy and creamy, not runny. If it stays thin, set the pan over a very low heat for 30 seconds at a time, tossing constantly so it does not scramble. For anyone who needs to avoid lightly cooked eggs, use pasteurised eggs.
Serve straight away with extra cheese and black pepper.

ingredientsStructured.name: Parmesan or Pecorino
ingredientsStructured.note: finely grated, plus extra to serve

recipes.title: Spinach and ricotta cannelloni
ingredients: 50 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the passata, oregano and half the salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Put the spinach in a colander and pour over a kettle of boiling water to wilt it. Cool slightly, then squeeze out as much water as you can and chop finely.
In a mixing bowl, mix the spinach, ricotta, most of the hard cheese, the egg, lemon zest, nutmeg and remaining salt.

Spread a third of the tomato sauce over the base of a baking dish. Spoon or pipe the filling into the cannelloni tubes and lay them in a single layer on the sauce. Pour over the remaining sauce, making sure the pasta is covered.

Top with the mozzarella and the rest of the hard cheese. Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the pasta is tender when pierced with a knife, the sauce is bubbling and the filling is piping hot in the centre.
To batch cook, assemble, cool, cover and freeze. Defrost overnight in the fridge and bake until piping hot throughout.

recipes.title: Stuffed peppers with rice and beans
ingredients: 4 large red peppers, halved lengthways and deseeded
240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Cook the rice in a saucepan according to the packet instructions, then drain.
Rub the pepper halves with 1 tbsp of the oil, sit them cut-side up in a baking dish and roast for 10 minutes to soften.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, tomatoes, sweetcorn, salt and cooked rice and heat through for 3 minutes. Stir in half the cheese.
Pack the filling into the peppers, scatter over the remaining cheese and bake for 20–25 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the cheese is golden. Scatter with coriander to serve.

recipes.title: Swedish-style meatballs
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
4 tbsp lingonberry or cranberry sauce, optional
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk in a mixing bowl for 5 minutes. Add both minces, the egg, onion, allspice and half the salt and mix well. Roll into about 24 small balls. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Put the potatoes in a large pot of salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 15–18 minutes until tender.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the meatballs for 10–12 minutes, turning, until browned all over and cooked through to 71°C with no pink remaining. Lift onto a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the stock and simmer for 3 minutes until thickened, then stir in the cream and remaining salt.
Return the meatballs to the gravy and simmer gently for 3 minutes to heat through.
Drain and mash the potatoes (or serve them boiled) and spoon over the meatballs and gravy, with lingonberry or cranberry sauce if using.

recipes.title: Sweet and sour pork
ingredients: 550 g pork tenderloin, trimmed and cut into bite-sized chunks
2 bell peppers, deseeded and cut into chunks
435 g canned pineapple chunks in juice, drained, juice reserved
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Toss the pork with 2 tbsp of the cornflour and the salt in a mixing bowl. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw pork.
Whisk 150 ml of the reserved pineapple juice with the rice vinegar, sugar, tomato purée, tamari and remaining cornflour in a jug to make the sauce.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the pork in batches for 5–6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp and cooked to at least 63°C. Lift onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion and peppers for 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic and pineapple for 1 minute, then pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Return the pork, toss to coat and serve straight away with the rice. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

ingredientsStructured.name: pork tenderloin
ingredientsStructured.note: trimmed and cut into bite-sized chunks

recipes.title: Teriyaki chicken with rice
ingredients: 600 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger and cornflour with 3 tbsp water in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 7–8 minutes, turning, until golden. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy and the chicken reaches 74°C with no pink remaining.
Meanwhile, steam or boil the broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender.

Serve the chicken and sauce over the rice with the broccoli, topped with sesame seeds and spring onions if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Thai-style fishcakes
ingredients: 500 g skinless white fish fillets, such as cod or haddock, roughly chopped
60 g green beans, very thinly sliced
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan according to the packet instructions and keep warm.
Put the fish, curry paste, egg, fish sauce and cornflour in a food processor and pulse until it forms a thick, sticky paste. Do not over-blend.

Transfer to a mixing bowl and stir in the spring onions, green beans and coriander. With wet hands, shape into 12 small patties about 1.5 cm thick, and wash your hands after handling the raw fish mixture.

Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry half the fishcakes for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (63°C in the centre, firm and opaque when cut). Repeat with the remaining oil and fishcakes.
Serve with the rice, cucumber, sweet chilli sauce for dipping and lime wedges.

ingredientsStructured.name: skinless white fish fillets
ingredientsStructured.note: such as cod or haddock, roughly chopped

recipes.title: Thai green chicken curry
ingredients: 600 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
150 g green beans, trimmed and halved
1 small bunch fresh basil or coriander, leaves picked, optional
steps: Rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok or large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the curry paste and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the paste, cooking for 3 minutes. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and pepper and simmer for 5–6 minutes until the vegetables are just tender and the chicken reaches 74°C with no pink remaining.

Stir in the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice, then taste and adjust. Serve over the rice, topped with basil or coriander if using. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

ingredientsStructured.name: small bunch fresh basil or coriander

recipes.title: Three-bean vegetable chilli
ingredients: 240 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
240 g canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and pepper for 10 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, chilli powder and oregano and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Stir in the tomato purée for 1 minute more.
Add the tomatoes, all the beans, the stock and the salt. Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in a saucepan according to the packet instructions.
Serve the chilli over the rice with lime wedges and coriander, if you like.

This doubles easily. Cool leftover chilli quickly and refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze in portions. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Tofu and vegetable stir-fry
ingredients: 450 g extra-firm tofu, drained and patted dry
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan according to the packet instructions and keep warm.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and toss in a mixing bowl with 2 tsp of the cornflour. In a small bowl, mix the tamari, maple syrup, vinegar, sesame oil, water and remaining cornflour to make the sauce.
Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 8–10 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden on all sides. Lift onto a plate.

Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli, pepper and carrot for 3 minutes. Add the mangetout, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 2 minutes more, until the vegetables are just tender but still crisp.
Stir the sauce, pour it into the wok and bubble for 1 minute until glossy. Return the tofu, toss to coat, then scatter with spring onions and sesame seeds. Serve with the rice.

recipes.title: Turkey chilli
ingredients: 240 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over a medium heat. Add the onion, pepper and carrot and cook for 8 minutes until softened.
Turn up the heat, add the turkey mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Stir in the garlic, chilli powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, kidney beans, stock and salt. Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. The turkey should reach 74°C with no pink remaining.
Serve with rice or jacket potatoes and lime wedges if using. Cool leftovers quickly and freeze in portions for up to 3 months; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Turkey meatballs in tomato sauce
steps: Mix the turkey mince, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, oregano and half the salt in a mixing bowl. Shape into about 20 walnut-sized balls. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw mince.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and brown the meatballs for 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden all over. Lift onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, sugar and remaining salt.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs reach 74°C in the centre with no pink remaining.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water according to the packet, then drain.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the spaghetti, topped with basil if using. Cooked meatballs in sauce freeze well; reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Vegetable chow mein
steps: Cook the noodles in a saucepan according to the packet instructions, then drain, rinse under cold water and toss with the sesame oil so they don't stick.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cornflour and water in a small bowl to make the sauce.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the pepper, carrot and mushrooms for 3 minutes, then add the edamame, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes until the edamame are hot through.
Add the noodles, beansprouts and spring onions, pour over the sauce and toss for 2–3 minutes until everything is coated, glossy and piping hot. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Vegetable korma
ingredients: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, garam masala, turmeric and cinnamon and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the carrots, cauliflower and chickpeas and stir to coat in the spices. Pour in the coconut milk and stock, add the ground almonds, sugar and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender. Add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook in a saucepan according to the packet instructions.
Serve the korma over the rice with coriander. Leftover korma freezes well; reheat until steaming hot. Cool leftover rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Vegetable lasagne
ingredients: 240 g canned green lentils, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, courgettes, pepper and mushrooms for 10 minutes until softened and any liquid has evaporated. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato purée, lentils, oregano, half the salt and the pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.

Meanwhile, make the white sauce: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until smooth and thick. Season with the nutmeg and remaining salt.

Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). In a baking dish about 20 x 30 cm, layer a third of the vegetable sauce, then a layer of lasagne sheets, then a quarter of the white sauce. Repeat twice, then finish with the remaining white sauce and scatter over the cheese.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling and a knife slides easily through the pasta. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days or can be frozen in portions; reheat until piping hot throughout.

recipes.title: Sesame chicken noodle salad
ingredients: 500 g skinless chicken breasts, cut into thin strips
steps: Whisk 3 tbsp of the soy sauce with the sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, ginger and garlic in a large mixing bowl to make the dressing.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 6–8 minutes until golden and the thickest piece reaches 74°C. Add the remaining soy sauce and toss. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in a saucepan of boiling water according to the pack instructions. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Add the noodles, carrots, pepper and most of the spring onions to the dressing and toss well.
Top with the chicken, remaining spring onions, sesame seeds and coriander if using. Serve warm or cold.

recipes.title: Beef and bean burritos
ingredients: 240 g canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the beef mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Wash your hands after handling the raw mince.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and the mince reaches 71°C with no pink remaining.

Warm the tortillas, then fill each with rice, beef, cheese, lettuce and soured cream if using. Fold in the ends and roll up tightly. Leftover filling can be cooled within an hour and frozen for up to three months; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Beetroot and feta salad with walnuts
ingredients: 500 g cooked beetroot, not in vinegar, cut into wedges
240 g canned green lentils, drained and rinsed
10 g fresh mint, leaves torn, optional
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, shaking the pan, until fragrant. Cool and roughly chop.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, honey, mustard, salt and pepper together in a large mixing bowl.
Add the lentils and rocket and toss gently in the dressing.
Spread over a platter and arrange the beetroot wedges on top so they do not stain everything pink.
Crumble over the feta, scatter with the walnuts and mint if using, and serve.

ingredientsStructured.name: cooked beetroot
ingredientsStructured.note: not in vinegar, cut into wedges

recipes.title: BLT sandwich
steps: Heat the grill to high. Lay the bacon on the grill rack and cook for 3–4 minutes each side until crisp and golden. Wash your hands after handling the raw bacon.
Toast the bread lightly under the grill or in a toaster.
Spread mayonnaise over one side of each slice.
Layer lettuce, tomato and three slices of bacon on four of the slices, season with pepper and top with the remaining bread.
Press down gently, cut in half with a sharp knife and serve while the bacon is warm.

recipes.title: Cheese and onion quiche
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin with the pastry, pressing it into the edges and leaving the excess overhanging. Chill for 10 minutes.

Line the pastry with baking paper and baking beans and bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more until pale golden. Trim the edge with a knife and reduce the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan over medium-low heat and cook the onions for 10–12 minutes until soft and golden. Leave to cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, salt, pepper and nutmeg in a jug. Scatter the onions and most of the cheese over the pastry case, pour in the egg mixture and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and just set in the centre (71°C) with a slight wobble. Cool for 15 minutes before slicing. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to three days.

recipes.title: Chicken and avocado wrap
ingredients: 500 g skinless chicken breasts, cut into strips
steps: Toss the chicken strips with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt in a bowl.

Cook the chicken in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning often, until golden and the thickest piece reaches 74°C with juices running clear. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Meanwhile, mash the avocados with the lime juice and a pinch of salt in a bowl until fairly smooth.
Warm the tortillas in the dry pan for 20 seconds each side so they fold without cracking.
Spread avocado down the middle of each tortilla, add lettuce, tomato, chicken, cheese and a spoonful of soured cream if using. Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and cut in half with a knife.

recipes.title: Chicken Caesar salad
ingredients: 150 g ciabatta, torn into bite-sized pieces
2 romaine lettuces, leaves separated and roughly chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the ciabatta pieces with 2 tbsp of the oil on a baking tray and bake for 8–10 minutes until golden and crisp.

Rub the chicken with the remaining oil, salt and pepper. Cook in a large frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes each side until the thickest part reaches 74°C and the juices run clear. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
For the dressing, whisk the mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, half the Parmesan and the water in a small bowl until smooth.
Put the lettuce in a large mixing bowl, add most of the dressing and toss until every leaf is coated.
Divide the lettuce between plates, top with the sliced chicken and croutons, drizzle over the rest of the dressing and finish with the remaining Parmesan.

recipes.title: Chicken and pepper quesadillas
ingredients: 400 g skinless chicken breasts, cut into small strips
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, paprika, cumin and salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.

Add the peppers and onion and cook for another 5–6 minutes until the vegetables soften and the chicken reaches 74°C with juices running clear. Tip into a bowl and wipe the pan. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Lay the tortillas flat. Scatter half of each with cheese, then the chicken mixture, then a little more cheese. Fold over into half-moons.
Cook the quesadillas one or two at a time in the dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes each side, pressing with a spatula, until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and soured cream if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken pitta with tzatziki
steps: Mix the oil, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, half the salt and the pepper in a bowl. Add the chicken, turn to coat and leave to marinate for 15 minutes. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
For the tzatziki, squeeze the grated cucumber in a clean tea towel to remove excess water. Mix with the yogurt, remaining garlic, remaining lemon juice, mint and remaining salt.

Heat a griddle pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes each side until charred and the thickest part reaches 74°C with juices running clear. Rest for 3 minutes, then slice.
Warm the pitta breads in a toaster or the hot pan for a minute, then split open into pockets.
Fill each pitta with lettuce, tomato, onion and chicken, and spoon in plenty of tzatziki.

recipes.title: Chicken satay skewers with rice
ingredients: 600 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into strips
steps: Soak eight wooden skewers in water. Mix 3 tbsp of the tamari with the turmeric, coriander, sugar, half the garlic and the oil in a bowl. Add the chicken, coat well and marinate for 30 minutes in the fridge. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Rinse the rice, then cook in a saucepan with 450 ml water: bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes.

Heat the grill to high. Thread the chicken onto the skewers and lay on a foil-lined baking tray. Grill for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and the thickest piece reaches 74°C with juices running clear.

Meanwhile, warm the peanut butter, coconut milk, remaining tamari, remaining garlic, lime juice and chilli flakes in a small saucepan, stirring until smooth and glossy. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Serve the skewers on the rice with cucumber batons and the satay sauce for dipping. Cool any leftover rice within an hour and eat within a day.

recipes.title: Chicken Waldorf salad
steps: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add the salt. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 12–15 minutes until the thickest part reaches 74°C and the juices run clear. Leave to cool in the liquid for 10 minutes, then shred or dice. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant, then roughly chop.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper.
Toss the apple in the dressing straight away to stop it browning, then fold in the chicken, celery, grapes and most of the walnuts.
Spoon onto the lettuce leaves and scatter with the remaining walnuts and the chives if using.

recipes.title: Smashed chickpea sandwich
ingredients: 480 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Tip the chickpeas into a mixing bowl and roughly crush with a potato masher or fork, leaving some texture.
Stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, celery, spring onions, parsley, salt and pepper.
Taste and add a little more lemon juice or seasoning if needed.
Spread the mixture over four slices of bread, top with lettuce and tomato, and cover with the remaining bread.
Cut in half with a knife and serve. The filling keeps in the fridge for up to three days.

recipes.title: Cobb salad
steps: Rub the chicken with the oil, salt and pepper. Cook in a large frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes each side until the thickest part reaches 74°C and the juices run clear. Rest, then dice. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Cook the bacon in the same pan for 3–4 minutes each side until crisp, then drain on kitchen paper and break into pieces.
Meanwhile, simmer the eggs in a saucepan of boiling water for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Whisk the extra virgin olive oil, vinegar, mustard and honey with a pinch of salt to make the dressing.
Spread the lettuce over a large platter and arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in rows on top. Sprinkle with chives and drizzle with the dressing.

recipes.title: Cold sesame noodles
steps: Cook the noodles in a large saucepan of boiling water according to the pack instructions, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Drain and rinse under cold running water until completely cool, then drain well.
Whisk the tahini, peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup, garlic, ginger and warm water in a large mixing bowl until smooth and pourable.
Add the noodles and edamame and toss until coated, then add the cucumber, carrot and most of the spring onions.
Serve topped with the remaining spring onions, sesame seeds and a drizzle of chilli oil if you like. Keeps in the fridge for up to two days.

recipes.title: Sweetcorn and black bean salad
ingredients: 480 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large dry frying pan over high heat. Add the sweetcorn and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred. Tip into a large mixing bowl to cool.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin, chilli flakes and salt together.
Add the black beans, pepper, onion and tomatoes to the sweetcorn, pour over the dressing and toss.
Fold in the avocado and coriander just before serving.
Without the avocado, the salad keeps in the fridge for up to three days, so make a big batch for packed lunches.

recipes.title: Couscous salad with feta and mint
steps: Put the couscous in a large heatproof mixing bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, breaking up any clumps, and leave to cool for a few minutes.
Whisk the lemon zest and juice, olive oil, salt and pepper together, then stir through the couscous.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, spring onions, mint and parsley.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve. Keeps in the fridge for up to two days.

recipes.title: Egg mayonnaise sandwich
steps: Lower the eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm.
Drain and cool the eggs under cold running water for a few minutes, then peel.
Mash the eggs in a mixing bowl with a fork, then stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, chives, salt and pepper.
Butter the bread, spread the egg mixture over four slices, scatter with cress if using and top with the remaining bread.
Cut into halves or triangles with a knife. The filling keeps covered in the fridge for up to a day.

recipes.title: Fattoush salad
ingredients: 2 pitta breads, torn into bite-sized pieces
5 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
20 g fresh flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the pitta pieces with 1 tbsp of the oil and half the sumac on a baking tray and bake for 8–10 minutes until crisp and golden.
Whisk the remaining oil and sumac, the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic and salt in a small bowl.
Put the chickpeas, lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, radishes, pepper, spring onions, parsley and mint in a large mixing bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss well.
Add the crisp pitta just before serving and toss once more so it stays crunchy.

recipes.title: Tomato and mozzarella flatbread pizzas
ingredients: 300 g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Heat the oven to 240°C (fan 220°C) and put two large baking trays in to heat.
Mix the flour, yogurt and salt in a mixing bowl to a soft dough. Knead briefly on a floured surface until smooth, then divide into four and roll each into a thin oval.
Stir the passata with the garlic and oregano. Brush the hot baking trays with the oil and lay the flatbreads on them.
Spread the tomato sauce over the bases, then top with the mozzarella and cherry tomatoes.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the bases are crisp underneath and the cheese is bubbling. Scatter with basil if using and cut into slices.

recipes.title: Greek salad with chickpeas
ingredients: 480 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, half the oregano, salt and pepper together in a large mixing bowl.
Add the chickpeas and red onion and stir to coat. Leave for 5 minutes so the onion softens slightly in the dressing.
Use a sharp knife to prepare the tomatoes, cucumber and pepper, then add them to the bowl with the olives and toss gently.
Pile the salad onto plates. Break the feta into large chunks over the top and sprinkle with the remaining oregano.
Serve straight away, or keep undressed in the fridge for up to a day and add the feta just before eating.

recipes.title: Ham and cheese toastie
steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Place four slices butter side down on a board. Top each with a quarter of the cheese, two slices of ham, a little pepper and then the remaining cheese.
Cover with the remaining bread, butter side up.
Cook two sandwiches at a time in a large frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes each side, pressing down with a spatula, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Rest for a minute, then cut in half with a knife and serve.

recipes.title: Hummus and roasted vegetable wrap
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C). Spread the courgettes, peppers and onion on a large baking tray, toss with the oil, herbs, salt and pepper.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges. Squeeze over the lemon juice.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for about 20 seconds each side.
Spread a quarter of the hummus over each tortilla, leaving a border. Top with spinach and the warm vegetables.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and cut in half. Leftover roasted vegetables keep in the fridge for up to three days.

recipes.title: Korean-style beef lettuce cups
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Meanwhile, toss the carrots and cucumber with the rice vinegar and half the sugar in a bowl and leave to quick-pickle.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Brown the beef mince for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until crisp in places. Wash your hands after handling the raw mince.

Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then add the gochujang, soy sauce, remaining sugar and sesame oil. Cook for 2–3 minutes until sticky and the mince reaches 71°C with no pink remaining. Stir in most of the spring onions.
Spoon a little rice into each lettuce leaf, top with the beef and pickled vegetables, and finish with the remaining spring onions and sesame seeds if using.

recipes.title: Lentil salad with roasted peppers
ingredients: 3 red peppers, cut into wide strips
200 g dried green or Puy lentils, rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the peppers and onion with 1 tbsp of the oil on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes until soft and charred at the edges.
Meanwhile, put the lentils in a saucepan, cover generously with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender but still holding their shape. Drain well.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar, mustard, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper in a large mixing bowl.
Add the warm lentils to the dressing and stir so they soak it up, then fold in the roasted vegetables, tomatoes and parsley.
Toss through the rocket just before serving. Without the rocket, the salad keeps in the fridge for up to three days.

recipes.title: Niçoise salad
ingredients: 500 g baby new potatoes, halved if large
320 g canned tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot of cold salted water, bring to the boil and simmer for 12–15 minutes until tender. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water.
Meanwhile, lower the eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and simmer for 9 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel and cut into quarters.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper together to make the dressing.
Arrange the lettuce on a large platter. Toss the potatoes and beans with half the dressing and spread over the leaves.
Top with the tomatoes, flakes of tuna, olives, eggs and anchovies if using. Drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve.

recipes.title: Panzanella
ingredients: 250 g day-old ciabatta, torn into chunks
6 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
600 g ripe tomatoes, cut into chunks
240 g canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the bread with 2 tbsp of the oil on a baking tray and bake for 8–10 minutes until crisp outside but still a little chewy inside.
Put the tomatoes in a large mixing bowl with the salt and leave for 10 minutes to release their juices.
Whisk the remaining oil with the vinegar, garlic and pepper, then pour over the tomatoes.
Add the cucumber, pepper, onion, beans, capers and bread and toss well so the bread soaks up the juices.
Leave to stand for 10–15 minutes, then tear in the basil and serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Pesto pasta salad
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, for the pasta water
30 g pine nuts, lightly toasted, optional
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the salt. Cook the fusilli for 10–12 minutes until just tender.
Drain the pasta, rinse under cold water until cool, then drain well.
In a large mixing bowl, stir the pesto, olive oil and lemon juice together.
Add the pasta, tomatoes, mozzarella and spinach and toss until everything is coated.
Scatter with pine nuts if using. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to two days, making it good for packed lunches.

recipes.title: Prawn and avocado rice bowl
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Drain well.
Whisk the tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey and lime juice together to make the dressing.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the prawns, garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 3–4 minutes, turning, until the prawns are pink and opaque throughout. Wash your hands after handling the raw prawns.
Divide the rice and edamame between bowls and spoon over half the dressing.
Top with the prawns, avocado, carrot, cucumber and spring onions. Drizzle with the remaining dressing and scatter with sesame seeds if using.

recipes.title: Quinoa salad with roasted vegetables
ingredients: 500 g butternut squash, peeled and cubed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the squash, peppers, courgette and onion on a large baking tray with 2 tbsp of the oil, the cumin and half the salt. Roast for 30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelised.

Meanwhile, put the quinoa and water in a saucepan, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice and remaining salt in a large mixing bowl.
Add the quinoa, roasted vegetables, parsley and spinach and toss so the spinach wilts slightly.
Scatter with pumpkin seeds and serve warm or cold. Portions keep in the fridge for up to three days, so it is ideal for packed lunches.

recipes.title: Vietnamese-style rice noodle salad
ingredients: 400 g firm tofu, drained and patted dry
steps: Make the dressing by stirring the lime juice, tamari, sugar, water, chilli and garlic together in a jug until the sugar dissolves.

Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and toss with the cornflour. Fry in the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides. Spoon over 2 tbsp of the dressing and toss.
Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles in a saucepan of boiling water according to the pack instructions, usually 3–4 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Divide the lettuce and noodles between bowls and top with the carrot, cucumber, tofu, mint and coriander.
Pour over the remaining dressing and scatter with the peanuts just before serving.

recipes.title: Homemade sausage rolls
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the sausagemeat, onion, sage and pepper in a mixing bowl with your hands until evenly combined. Wash your hands after handling the raw meat.
Unroll the pastry on a lightly floured surface and cut in half lengthways. Shape the sausage mixture into two long logs and lay one along the centre of each strip.
Brush one long edge with beaten egg, fold the pastry over the filling and press to seal, then crimp with a fork. Cut each roll into six pieces with a sharp knife and place on the tray.

Brush with egg, snip a small slit in each top and bake for 22–25 minutes until deep golden and the filling reaches 71°C with no pink remaining. Unbaked rolls can be frozen and cooked from frozen for an extra 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Smoked mackerel and potato salad
ingredients: 300 g smoked mackerel fillets, skin removed
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot of cold water with the salt, bring to the boil and simmer for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain and leave to cool for 10 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the crème fraîche, horseradish sauce, lemon zest and juice, most of the dill and the pepper.
Add the warm potatoes and spring onions and stir gently to coat.
Flake the mackerel into large pieces with a fork, discarding any bones, and fold through the potatoes.
Serve on a bed of watercress, scattered with the remaining dill. Keeps in the fridge for up to a day.

recipes.title: Spinach and feta filo triangles
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Wilt the spinach in a large saucepan over medium heat with 1 tbsp of the oil, stirring, for 2–3 minutes. Tip into a sieve, cool, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible and chop.
Mix the spinach, spring onions, feta, egg, dill, nutmeg and pepper in a mixing bowl.

Cut each filo sheet lengthways into two strips, keeping the rest covered with a damp tea towel. Brush a strip with oil, put a heaped spoonful of filling at one end and fold over corner to corner into a triangle, continuing to the end of the strip. Repeat to make 12 triangles.
Put the triangles on the tray, brush with oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake for 20–25 minutes until crisp, golden and piping hot in the middle. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Baked sweet potatoes with black beans
ingredients: 480 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Prick the sweet potatoes all over with a fork, rub with 1 tbsp of the oil and bake on a baking tray for 50–60 minutes until completely soft in the middle.
About 15 minutes before they are ready, heat the remaining oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the black beans and a splash of water and cook for 5 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken. Stir in half the lime juice and the salt.
Mix the tomatoes, avocado, coriander and remaining lime juice in a small bowl.
Split the potatoes open with a knife, spoon in the beans and top with the tomato and avocado mixture, plus a spoonful of coconut yogurt if you like.

recipes.title: Tabbouleh with grilled halloumi
ingredients: 60 g fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
15 g fresh mint, leaves finely chopped
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
steps: Put the bulgur in a heatproof mixing bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and leave for 15 minutes until tender. Drain off any remaining water and spread out to cool.
Add the parsley, mint, tomatoes, cucumber and spring onions to the bulgur.
Whisk the lemon juice, 3 tbsp of the oil, the salt and pepper together, pour over the salad and toss well.
Heat a griddle pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Brush the halloumi with the remaining oil and cook for 1–2 minutes each side until golden with char lines.
Pile the tabbouleh onto plates and top with the hot halloumi. The tabbouleh keeps in the fridge for up to two days; grill the halloumi just before eating.

recipes.title: Teriyaki tofu rice bowl
ingredients: 450 g extra-firm tofu, drained and patted dry
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook in a saucepan with 375 ml water: bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 5 minutes.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and toss with all but 1 tsp of the cornflour. Fry in the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, whisk the tamari, mirin, maple syrup, water, garlic, ginger and remaining cornflour in a jug. Steam or boil the broccoli in a saucepan for 3–4 minutes until just tender.
Pour the sauce over the tofu and bubble for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy and the tofu is coated.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the tofu, broccoli, carrot and spring onions. Scatter with sesame seeds if using. Cool any leftover rice within an hour, refrigerate and eat within a day.

recipes.title: Tomato, mozzarella and basil ciabatta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Put the ciabatta halves cut side up on a baking tray and warm for 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp.
Rub the cut sides with the garlic, then drizzle with half the olive oil.
Layer the mozzarella and tomato slices over the bottom halves and return to the oven for 2–3 minutes, just until the cheese starts to soften.
Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with the remaining oil and the balsamic vinegar, and tuck in the basil leaves and rocket if using.
Press the tops on and cut in half with a bread knife to serve.

recipes.title: Tuna and sweetcorn sandwich
ingredients: 290 g canned tuna in spring water, drained
steps: Tip the tuna into a mixing bowl and break it up with a fork.
Stir in the sweetcorn, mayonnaise, spring onions, lemon juice and pepper until evenly combined.
Spread the butter thinly over one side of each slice of bread.
Divide the tuna mixture between four slices, top with cucumber and lettuce, then cover with the remaining bread.
Cut each sandwich in half with a sharp knife and serve. The filling keeps covered in the fridge for up to a day.

recipes.title: Turkey club sandwich
steps: Heat the grill to high. Cook the bacon on the grill rack for 3–4 minutes each side until crisp. Wash your hands after handling the raw bacon.
Toast the bread under the grill or in a toaster until golden on both sides.
Spread mayonnaise over one side of each slice. On four slices, layer turkey and lettuce, then add a second slice, mayonnaise side up.
Top with bacon, tomato and a grind of pepper, then finish with the last slices, mayonnaise side down.
Secure each stack with two cocktail sticks and cut into triangles with a sharp knife.

recipes.title: Warm potato and green bean salad
ingredients: 250 g green beans, trimmed and halved
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot of cold water with half the salt, bring to the boil and simmer for 12–15 minutes until tender when pierced with a knife.
Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain everything well.
Meanwhile, whisk the shallot, mustard, vinegar, oil, remaining salt and pepper in a large mixing bowl.
Tip the hot potatoes and beans into the dressing and toss gently so the warm potatoes soak it up.
Stir in the capers, parsley and chives and serve warm. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to two days.

recipes.title: Avocado toast with poached eggs
ingredients: 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, optional
steps: Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork, then mix in the lemon juice, chilli flakes, half the salt and the pepper.
Bring a large saucepan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar.

Crack each egg into a cup, stir the water to make a gentle swirl and slide the eggs in one at a time. Poach for 4–5 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Meanwhile, toast the sourdough.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Spread the avocado over the toast, top each slice with an egg, sprinkle with the remaining salt and drizzle with olive oil, if using.

recipes.title: Bacon and egg breakfast muffins
steps: Heat the grill to high. Lay the bacon on the grill rack and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until cooked through and crisp at the edges. Wash your hands after handling raw meat.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes, then flip and cook for 1 minute more. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Toast the muffin halves and spread lightly with butter.
Lay a slice of cheese on each muffin base, then add an egg and two slices of bacon.
Add ketchup, if using, top with the muffin lids and serve warm.

recipes.title: Baked oats with apple
ingredients: 1 tbsp coconut oil, melted, plus extra for greasing
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C) and grease a medium baking dish with a little coconut oil.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, salt and flaxseed in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in the almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla and melted coconut oil, then fold in most of the apple.
Pour into the baking dish, scatter over the remaining apple and the pecans, if using.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden on top and set, with no liquid pooling in the centre.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes, then spoon into bowls. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat until hot.

recipes.title: Banana bread
ingredients: 100 g butter, melted, plus extra for greasing
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Grease a 900 g loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Mash the bananas in a large mixing bowl until mostly smooth, then whisk in the melted butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add the flour, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt and fold together until no dry flour remains. Stir in the walnuts, if using.
Scrape the batter into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 50–55 minutes until risen and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely. Keep wrapped for up to 4 days, or freeze in slices.

recipes.title: Banana pancakes
steps: Peel the bananas and put them in a blender with the eggs, oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Blend until smooth, then leave to stand for 5 minutes to thicken slightly.
Heat a little of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Spoon in about 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake, leaving space between them. Cook for 2–3 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges look set.
Flip carefully with a thin spatula and cook for 1–2 minutes more until golden and cooked through with no wet batter in the middle.
Keep warm on a plate while you cook the rest, adding a little more oil as needed.
Serve topped with blueberries and a drizzle of maple syrup, if using.

recipes.title: Berry smoothie
steps: Put the berries, banana, almond milk, oats and chia seeds into a blender.
Blend on high for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Taste and blend in the maple syrup if you would like it sweeter, or add a splash more almond milk if it is too thick.
Pour into two glasses and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Bircher muesli
steps: Put the oats, apple juice and milk into a large mixing bowl and stir well.
Coarsely grate the apples, skin on, and toss with the lemon juice to stop them browning. Stir into the oats with the yogurt, honey and cinnamon.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 6 hours, until the oats are soft and creamy.
In the morning, stir and loosen with a splash more milk if needed.
Spoon into bowls and top with hazelnuts and raspberries, if using.
Keep any leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Blueberry muffins
ingredients: 2 tbsp demerara sugar, for sprinkling, optional
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, salt and sugar in a large mixing bowl.
In a jug, whisk the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and fold together with a spatula until just combined; do not overmix.
Gently fold in the blueberries, then divide the batter between the cases and sprinkle with demerara sugar, if using.
Bake for 20–22 minutes until risen, golden and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack. Keep in an airtight tin for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Breakfast burritos
ingredients: 240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Cut the potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the potatoes for 12–15 minutes, turning often, until golden and tender.
Add the pepper, spring onions and paprika and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the beans to warm through.

Beat the eggs with the salt in a mixing bowl. Push the vegetables to one side of the pan, pour the eggs into the space and stir gently until fully set with no liquid egg remaining, then mix everything together.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan or the microwave for a few seconds so they are pliable.
Divide the filling between the tortillas, top with cheese and salsa, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Serve straight away, or toast seam-side down in the dry pan for 1–2 minutes to seal.
To batch cook, cool the burritos, wrap individually and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in the oven at 180°C (fan 160°C) for 25–30 minutes until piping hot in the centre.

recipes.title: Breakfast quesadillas
ingredients: 1 red pepper, deseeded and finely diced
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt in a mixing bowl.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Cook the pepper and spring onions for 3 minutes until soft.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently for 2–3 minutes until fully set with no liquid egg remaining. Tip onto a plate and wipe out the pan.
Lay a tortilla in the dry pan, scatter a quarter of the cheese over half of it, top with a quarter of the eggs and fold over.
Cook for 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp and the cheese has melted. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
Cut each quesadilla into wedges with a knife and serve with salsa, if using.

recipes.title: Cheese and chive scones
ingredients: 350 g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
170 ml milk, plus extra for brushing
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and mustard powder in a large mixing bowl. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in most of the cheese and the chives. Pour in the milk and mix with a table knife into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Tip onto a floured surface, knead very briefly and pat out to about 3 cm thick. Cut out rounds with a 6 cm cutter, re-pressing the trimmings to use it all.
Put on the baking tray, brush the tops with milk and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until well risen and golden and they sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool on a wire rack and eat warm or the same day, or freeze for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Chicken congee
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear.
Put the rice, stock, water and ginger in a large pot and bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, partly covered.

Add the whole chicken thighs and simmer for 20 minutes until cooked through: the thickest part should reach 74°C and the juices run clear. Lift out onto a board and wash your hands and the board after handling raw chicken.
Keep the rice simmering for a further 40–50 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick, until broken down into a thick, creamy porridge. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Shred the chicken with two forks, stir it back into the pot with the salt and white pepper, and remove the ginger slices.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onions, tamari and sesame oil.
To keep leftovers, cool within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours; reheat with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.title: Cooked breakfast traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the potatoes with half the oil and the salt in a large roasting tin or baking tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Add the sausages to the tin and roast for 10 minutes more.
Toss the mushrooms and tomatoes with the remaining oil, add to the tin with the bacon laid on top, and roast for 10 minutes until the bacon is crisp and the sausages are browned.
Check the sausages are cooked through: they should reach 71°C in the centre with no pink remaining. Wash your hands after handling raw meat.

Make four gaps in the tin and crack an egg into each. Return to the oven for 6–8 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Season with pepper, scatter with parsley, if using, and serve straight from the tin.

recipes.title: Cottage cheese pancakes
ingredients: 100 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Tip the cottage cheese into a sieve and press out as much liquid as you can, then put it in a mixing bowl and mash with a fork until fairly smooth.
Beat in the eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt, then stir in the flour to make a soft, thick mixture.
With floured hands, shape into 12 small patties about 2 cm thick and dust lightly with flour.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Fry the pancakes in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and firm in the centre.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve warm with soured cream and raspberries, if using.

recipes.title: Crêpes
ingredients: 30 g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
2 tbsp caster sugar, for sprinkling, optional
steps: Sift the flour, salt and sugar into a mixing bowl and make a well in the centre.

Add the eggs and a little of the milk and whisk, gradually drawing in the flour and adding the rest of the milk until you have a smooth batter like single cream. Whisk in the melted butter and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a crêpe pan or medium non-stick frying pan over medium heat and wipe with a little butter on kitchen paper.
Pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter and swirl quickly to coat the base thinly. Cook for 1 minute until the edges lift and the underside is lightly golden.
Flip with a spatula and cook for 30 seconds more. Stack on a plate and repeat, greasing the pan as needed; you should get about 12 crêpes.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of sugar, if using, or your favourite filling.
