ingredientsStructured.note: melted, plus extra for the pan

recipes.title: Eggs Benedict
ingredients: 125 g unsalted butter, melted and warm
steps: For the hollandaise, use pasteurised egg yolks. Put the yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water.
Whisk constantly while slowly pouring in the warm melted butter until the sauce is thick and glossy and reaches 71°C on a thermometer. Season with salt and cayenne, take off the heat and keep warm.
Warm the ham in a dry frying pan for 1 minute per side and toast the muffin halves.
Bring a large saucepan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup and slide in, four at a time.

Poach for 4–5 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Top each muffin half with a slice of ham and a poached egg, spoon over the hollandaise and scatter with chives, if using. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Fluffy pancakes
ingredients: 40 g butter, melted, plus extra for frying
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together in a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre.
In a jug, whisk the milk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the well and whisk gently until just combined; a few small lumps are fine. Rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake. Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles pop on the surface and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more until risen and cooked through in the middle. Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.
Serve stacked with maple syrup and berries, if using.

recipes.title: French toast
ingredients: 8 slices thick white bread, preferably a day old
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and salt together in a wide shallow dish.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat and add a knob of the butter.
Dip two slices of bread into the egg mixture for about 10 seconds per side so they soak it up without falling apart.
Fry for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden and the centre feels firm, with no runny egg mixture left inside.
Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the remaining slices, adding more butter as needed.
Serve with strawberries and maple syrup, if using.

recipes.title: Greek yogurt parfait
steps: Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla together in a mixing bowl until smooth.
Halve any large berries, such as strawberries, with a small knife.
Spoon a layer of yogurt into four glasses or bowls, then add a layer of berries and a layer of granola.
Repeat the layers, finishing with berries and a final sprinkle of granola.
Scatter with pistachios, if using, and serve straight away so the granola stays crunchy.

recipes.title: Homemade granola
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the oats, nuts, seeds, cinnamon and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Whisk the melted coconut oil, maple syrup and vanilla together, pour over the dry ingredients and stir until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the mixture out on the baking tray in an even layer and bake for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and toasty.
Leave to cool completely on the tray; it will crisp up as it cools. Stir through the raisins.
Store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks. Serve with plant-based milk or yogurt and fruit.

recipes.title: Huevos rancheros
ingredients: 1 green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, chilli and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Stir in the beans and lime juice and keep warm.
Warm the tortillas in a dry large frying pan for 30 seconds per side, then wrap in a clean tea towel.

Heat the remaining oil in the frying pan over medium heat and crack in the eggs. Fry for 3–4 minutes, spooning a little hot oil over the tops. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Lay two overlapping tortillas on each plate, spoon over the bean and tomato sauce and top with a fried egg.
Finish with avocado and coriander, if using, and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Kedgeree
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water for 10–12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Meanwhile, lower the eggs into a small saucepan of boiling water and cook for 10 minutes until hard-boiled. Cool under cold water, peel and cut into quarters.

Put the haddock and bay leaf in a large frying pan, cover with water and simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the fish reaches 63°C, is opaque and flakes easily. Lift out, discard the skin and any bones, and flake into large pieces.
Wipe out the frying pan, heat the oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the turmeric, cumin, coriander and chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Add the peas and cook for 2 minutes, then fold in the rice until coloured all over and piping hot.
Gently fold through the haddock, lemon juice and most of the parsley. Top with the eggs and remaining parsley and serve with lemon wedges, if using.
To keep leftovers, cool within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours; reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.title: Mango chia pudding
steps: Whisk the chia seeds, coconut milk, almond milk, maple syrup and vanilla in a mixing bowl.
Leave for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until thick and spoonable.
Roughly chop one mango and blend with the lime juice in a blender until smooth. Dice the other mango with a knife.
Layer the chia pudding and mango purée in four glasses, top with diced mango and coconut flakes, if using.
Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Mushrooms on toast
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave for 2 minutes to brown, then stir and cook for 5–6 minutes more until golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Turn the heat down to medium, add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with the salt and pepper, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Meanwhile, toast the sourdough.
Pile the mushrooms onto the toast, spooning over any pan juices, and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Overnight oats
steps: In a large mixing bowl, stir together the oats, chia seeds, almond milk, coconut yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla and salt until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture between four jars or lidded containers and press half the berries into the tops.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 6 hours, so the oats soften and thicken.
In the morning, stir each jar, loosening with a splash more almond milk if you like, and top with the remaining berries and the almonds.
Keep any extra jars in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Porridge with berries
ingredients: 250 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen
steps: Put the oats, almond milk, water, salt and cinnamon into a medium saucepan and stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then turn the heat down and cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Add a splash more water if it gets too stiff.
Meanwhile, if using frozen berries, warm them in a small saucepan over low heat for 3–4 minutes until juicy.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, top with the berries and drizzle with maple syrup.
Scatter over the seeds, if using, and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Potato breakfast frittata
steps: Cut the potatoes into 5 mm slices. Heat the oil in a 24 cm ovenproof non-stick frying pan over medium heat and cook the potatoes and onion, partly covered, for 15 minutes, turning often, until tender.
Add the pepper and cook for 4 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Heat the grill to medium-high.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pepper and parsley in a mixing bowl, then pour over the vegetables and gently shake the pan to spread evenly.
Cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes until the edges and base are set.
Slide the pan under the grill for 3–5 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre (71°C), with no liquid egg when cut.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and are good cold.

recipes.title: Scrambled eggs on toast
ingredients: 30 g butter, plus extra for spreading
steps: Crack the eggs into a mixing bowl, add the milk, salt and pepper, and beat with a fork until evenly combined.
Melt the butter in a non-stick saucepan over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula, scraping the base and sides, for 4–5 minutes until softly set curds form.
Meanwhile, toast the bread and spread with a little butter.
Take the pan off the heat when the eggs are just set with no liquid egg remaining, then spoon onto the toast.
Scatter over the chives, if using, and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion and peppers and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Tip in the tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Make six hollows in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each.

Cover the pan and cook over low heat for 7–10 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Scatter with coriander, if using, and serve hot straight from the pan.

recipes.title: Spinach and feta omelette
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper in a mixing bowl.
Heat half the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add the spinach and stir for 1–2 minutes until wilted, then tip onto a plate and squeeze out any excess liquid.
Add the remaining oil to the pan, pour in half the egg and swirl to cover the base. Cook for 1 minute, drawing the edges into the centre with a spatula so the runny egg flows underneath.
When the omelette is almost set, scatter half the spinach and feta over one side and cook for 1–2 minutes more until the egg is fully set with no liquid remaining.
Fold the omelette in half, slide onto a plate and sprinkle with oregano, if using.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients to make a second omelette.

recipes.title: Sweet potato breakfast hash
ingredients: 240 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Cut the sweet potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes with a sharp knife.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Add the sweet potato, cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Uncover, add the onion and pepper and cook for 8–10 minutes more until the potato is tender and crisp at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, cumin and salt and cook for 1 minute, then add the beans and warm through.

Make four hollows in the hash and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs.
Scatter with spring onions, if using, and serve from the pan.

recipes.title: Tofu scramble
steps: Pat the tofu dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, turmeric and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with your hands into rough, scrambled-egg-sized pieces.
Stir in the nutritional yeast, salt and pepper and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the tofu is hot and evenly golden.
Add the tomatoes and spinach and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach has wilted. Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Turkish eggs with garlic yogurt
ingredients: 400 g Greek yogurt, at room temperature
steps: Stir the yogurt, garlic and salt together in a mixing bowl, then spread over four shallow bowls.
Bring a large saucepan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup and slide them in, four at a time.

Poach for 4–5 minutes. Cook until the whites are fully set; for young children, pregnant people or anyone vulnerable, cook until the yolks are firm too, or use pasteurised eggs. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat until foaming, then stir in the chilli flakes and paprika and take off the heat.
Sit two eggs on each bowl of yogurt, spoon over the spiced butter and scatter with dill.
Serve straight away with toasted gluten-free bread for dipping, if using.

recipes.title: Vegetable egg muffins
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for greasing
1 red pepper, deseeded and finely diced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C) and generously grease a 12-hole muffin tin with oil.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the pepper and spring onions for 4 minutes until soft. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then take off the heat.
Whisk the eggs, salt, pepper and oregano in a large jug or mixing bowl.
Divide the vegetables and cherry tomatoes between the muffin holes, then pour over the egg mixture to fill each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 18–22 minutes until puffed and set in the centre (71°C), with no liquid egg when pierced with a knife.
Cool for 5 minutes, then run a knife around each one to release. Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat until piping hot, or freeze for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Waffles
steps: Heat a waffle iron and lightly brush the plates with oil.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large mixing bowl.
In a jug, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla, then pour into the dry ingredients and whisk until just smooth.
Pour enough batter into the waffle iron to cover the plates, close and cook for 4–5 minutes until crisp, golden and no longer steaming heavily.
Keep the waffles warm on a wire rack in a low oven while you cook the rest.
Serve with berries and maple syrup, if using. To batch cook, cool leftover waffles, freeze in a bag for up to 2 months and reheat in a toaster until hot through.

recipes.title: Apple crumble
ingredients: 4 large cooking apples, peeled, cored and sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C).
Toss the apple slices with the caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice, then spread them over the base of a medium ovenproof dish.
Put the flour in a mixing bowl and rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in the demerara sugar.
Scatter the crumble evenly over the apples without pressing it down.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until the top is golden and the fruit is bubbling up at the edges and soft when pierced with a knife.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes, then serve warm with custard if you like. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Baked apples
ingredients: 4 large apples, such as Bramley or Braeburn
150 g natural yogurt, to serve, optional
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).
Core the apples with an apple corer or small knife, leaving them whole. Score a thin line around the middle of each apple so the skin does not burst.
Mix the sultanas, sugar, cinnamon and butter together in a small bowl, then pack the mixture firmly into the hollow centre of each apple.
Stand the apples in a small ovenproof dish and pour the water around them.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, spooning the juices over halfway through, until the apples are soft right through when tested with a knife.
Serve warm with the syrupy juices and a spoonful of yogurt if you like.

recipes.title: Banana nice cream
ingredients: 30 g dairy-free dark chocolate, grated, to serve, optional
steps: Spread the banana slices in a single layer on a lined baking tray and freeze for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until solid.
Put the frozen banana in a blender or food processor with the coconut milk and vanilla. Leave for 2–3 minutes to soften slightly.
Blend, stopping to scrape down the sides often, until the banana breaks down from crumbs into a thick, smooth soft-serve. Add the maple syrup if you want it sweeter.
Serve straight away topped with grated chocolate if you like, or spoon into a container and freeze for 1 hour for a firmer scoop. Eat within a week; let it soften for 10 minutes before scooping.

recipes.title: Bread and butter pudding
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (fan 150°C). Use a little of the butter to grease a medium ovenproof dish.
Butter the bread on one side, cut each slice into triangles and arrange them, buttered side up and overlapping, in the dish, scattering the sultanas between the layers.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the milk, cream, eggs, caster sugar and vanilla until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread and leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Grate the nutmeg over the top and sprinkle with the demerara sugar.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until puffed and golden and the custard is set in the centre (71°C); it should not wobble like liquid when you shake the dish gently.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers and eat within 2 days, reheating until piping hot.

recipes.title: Carrot cake
ingredients: 250 g carrots, peeled and coarsely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Grease two 20 cm round sandwich tins and line the bases with baking paper.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the oil, brown sugar and eggs until smooth. Add the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and ginger and stir until just combined.
Fold in the grated carrots, sultanas and most of the walnuts, keeping a small handful back for the top.

Divide between the tins and bake for 30–35 minutes until risen and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the butter and icing sugar together until smooth, then beat in the cream cheese and vanilla briefly until thick and creamy; do not overbeat or it will turn runny.
Sandwich the cakes with half the frosting, spread the rest over the top and scatter with the reserved walnuts. Store in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Cherry clafoutis
ingredients: 15 g unsalted butter, softened, for greasing
1 tsp icing sugar, for dusting, optional
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Butter a medium ovenproof dish generously and spread the cherries over the base.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar until frothy, then whisk in the flour until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the milk, vanilla and salt to make a thin, smooth batter.
Pour the batter over the cherries and bake for 35–40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre (71°C); a knife pushed into the middle should come out clean.
Leave to cool for 10 minutes; it will sink a little, which is normal. Dust with icing sugar if you like and serve warm. Refrigerate leftovers and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Chocolate brownies
ingredients: 200 g dark chocolate, broken into pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Grease and line a 20 cm square baking tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a saucepan over a very low heat, stirring until smooth. Take off the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the sugar and eggs for 2–3 minutes until pale and slightly thickened, then stir in the melted chocolate mixture.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and salt and fold gently until no dry streaks remain.
Pour into the tin, level the top and bake for 25–30 minutes until the top is shiny and crackly and the centre is just set; a skewer should come out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 16 squares. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Chocolate chip cookies
ingredients: 150 g milk or dark chocolate chips
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C) and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter and both sugars together in a mixing bowl until light and creamy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt until just combined, then mix in the chocolate chips.
Roll the dough into 16 balls and space them well apart on the trays, flattening each one slightly.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
Leave on the trays for 5 minutes to firm up, then move to a wire rack to cool. Keep in an airtight tin for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Chocolate-dipped strawberries
ingredients: 150 g dairy-free dark chocolate, broken into pieces
steps: Wash the strawberries and dry them thoroughly with kitchen paper; any water will stop the chocolate sticking. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Put the chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water. Stir until just melted and smooth, then take off the heat.
Holding each strawberry by the stalk, dip it about two-thirds of the way into the chocolate, let the excess drip off and lay it on the tray.
Chill in the fridge for about 30 minutes until the chocolate has set.
Serve the same day for the best texture, keeping them in the fridge until needed.

recipes.title: Chocolate mousse
steps: This mousse is made with whipped cream instead of eggs, so there is no raw egg. Put the chocolate in a heatproof mixing bowl.

Heat 100 ml of the cream in a small saucepan until it just starts to steam, then pour it over the chocolate. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir until smooth and glossy. Stir in the vanilla and salt and leave to cool to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whip the remaining cream with the sugar until it holds soft peaks.
Fold a large spoonful of whipped cream into the chocolate to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest until evenly combined with no white streaks.
Spoon into four small glasses or ramekins, cover and chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours until set.
Serve topped with raspberries if you like. Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Crème caramel
ingredients: 150 g caster sugar, for the caramel
50 g caster sugar, for the custard
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (fan 130°C). Stand six ramekins in a deep roasting tin.

Put the sugar for the caramel and the water in a small saucepan and heat gently without stirring until the sugar dissolves, then boil, swirling the pan, until it turns a deep amber. Quickly pour into the ramekins and tilt to coat the bases. Take care, as hot caramel burns badly.

Warm the milk in a saucepan until steaming. In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs, yolks, sugar for the custard and vanilla, then slowly whisk in the warm milk. Strain into a jug and pour into the ramekins.
Pour hot water from the kettle into the roasting tin to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 40–45 minutes until the custards are set in the centre (71°C) with just a slight wobble. Lift out of the water and cool.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight. To serve, run a knife around each custard and turn out onto a plate so the caramel pools around it. Eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Eggless tiramisu
ingredients: 250 ml strong coffee, freshly brewed and cooled
steps: This tiramisu uses whipped cream and mascarpone instead of raw eggs. Shop-bought sponge fingers usually contain baked egg, so check the pack if you need to avoid egg completely. It contains coffee, so it is not suitable for young children.
Pour the cooled coffee into a shallow dish and stir in the coffee liqueur if using; leave it out for an alcohol-free version.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the mascarpone, cream, icing sugar and vanilla together until thick and holding soft peaks. Do not overwhip.
Dip half the sponge fingers into the coffee, one at a time, for a second on each side, and lay them in a single layer in a dish about 20 cm square. Spread half the cream over the top.
Repeat with the remaining sponge fingers and cream, smoothing the top.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight, so it firms up and the flavours develop. Dust generously with cocoa powder through a sieve just before serving. Eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Fresh fruit bowl with honey and lime
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh mint leaves, shredded, optional
steps: Wash all the fruit and pat dry. Use a sharp knife to prepare the strawberries, grapes, mango and kiwi as listed.
In a small bowl, whisk the lime zest, lime juice and honey together until the honey dissolves.
Put all the fruit in a large mixing bowl, pour over the dressing and toss gently so the softer fruit does not break up.
Leave to stand for 10 minutes so the juices mingle, then scatter with mint if using and serve. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Sticky gingerbread
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C). Grease and line a 20 cm square baking tin with baking paper.
Put the butter, sugar, golden syrup and treacle in a saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until melted and smooth. Take off the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda. Pour in the melted mixture, milk and eggs and whisk until you have a smooth, runny batter.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40–45 minutes until risen, firm to the touch and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 16 squares. It gets stickier if wrapped and kept for a day; store in an airtight tin for up to a week.

recipes.title: Lemon drizzle cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper.
In a mixing bowl, beat the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, adding a spoonful of the flour with each to stop the mixture curdling.
Fold in the remaining flour, the baking powder, milk and lemon zest until smooth, then spoon into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until risen, golden and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, stir the lemon juice and granulated sugar together in a small bowl.

As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, prick it all over with a skewer and spoon the lemon sugar evenly over the top. Leave to cool completely in the tin so the drizzle soaks in and sets into a crisp crust, then slice.

recipes.title: Lemon posset
ingredients: 2 large lemons, finely zested and juiced
steps: Put the cream and sugar in a saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to the boil and let it bubble for exactly 3 minutes, stirring so it does not catch or boil over.
Take off the heat and stir in the lemon zest and juice; you need about 75 ml juice. The mixture will thicken slightly. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Pour through a sieve into a jug, then divide between four small glasses or ramekins.
Cool, then cover and chill in the fridge for at least 3 hours until set. Top with raspberries if you like. Keep in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: No-bake strawberry cheesecake
ingredients: 500 g full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
steps: Line the base of a 20 cm springform tin with baking paper.

Crush the biscuits to fine crumbs in a food bag with a rolling pin, or in a blender. Melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the crumbs, then press firmly into the base of the tin. Chill while you make the filling.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese, icing sugar, vanilla and lemon zest until smooth.
In another bowl, whip the double cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the cream cheese mixture until evenly combined.
Spread the filling over the biscuit base and smooth the top. Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until firm.

Warm the jam with a teaspoon of water until runny, toss with the strawberries and arrange on top of the cheesecake. Release from the tin and slice with a knife dipped in hot water. Keep in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Vanilla panna cotta
ingredients: 2 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
steps: Soak the gelatine leaves in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until floppy.
Put the cream, milk and sugar in a saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is steaming but not boiling. Take off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Squeeze the excess water from the gelatine, add it to the warm cream and stir until completely dissolved.
Strain into a jug, then pour into six small moulds, ramekins or glasses.
Leave to cool, then cover and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set with a gentle wobble.
To turn out, dip each mould briefly in hot water and invert onto a plate. Serve with raspberries if you like. This dessert contains gelatine, so it is not suitable for vegetarians.

ingredientsStructured.name: vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract

recipes.title: Pavlova with summer berries
steps: Heat the oven to 140°C (fan 120°C). Draw a 22 cm circle on a sheet of baking paper, flip it over and put it on a baking tray.
In a spotlessly clean, grease-free mixing bowl, whisk the egg whites with an electric whisk until they form stiff peaks.
Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, whisking well after each addition, until the meringue is thick, glossy and the sugar has dissolved. Whisk in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Spoon the meringue onto the circle, making a slight hollow in the middle and higher sides.

Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until crisp and dry on the outside, then turn the oven off and leave the pavlova inside with the door ajar to cool completely, at least 1 hour. The meringue is fully baked, so there is no raw egg.
Just before serving, whip the cream to soft peaks, spread it over the pavlova and pile the berries on top. Serve straight away, as the meringue softens once topped.

recipes.title: Peach cobbler
ingredients: 500 g canned sliced peaches in juice, drained
2 tbsp caster sugar, for the fruit
50 g caster sugar, for the topping
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C).
Toss the peaches with the sugar for the fruit, cornflour, cinnamon and lemon juice, then spread them over the base of a medium ovenproof dish.

For the topping, mix the flour, sugar for the topping and baking powder in a mixing bowl. Rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the milk with a knife to make a soft, sticky dough.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough over the peaches, leaving small gaps between them, and sprinkle with the demerara sugar.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the topping is risen and golden, cooked through underneath, and the fruit is bubbling.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving warm. Refrigerate leftovers and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Poached pears
ingredients: 4 firm pears, peeled, stalks left on
1 lemon, zest pared into strips and juiced
steps: Put the water, sugar, cinnamon stick, star anise, vanilla, lemon zest and lemon juice in a saucepan just big enough to hold the pears. Heat gently, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Slice a thin piece off the base of each pear so it can stand up later, then lower the pears into the syrup.
Cover with a circle of baking paper to keep them submerged and simmer gently for 20–30 minutes, turning occasionally, until a knife slides easily into the thickest part.
Lift the pears out with a slotted spoon. Boil the syrup for 5–8 minutes until reduced by about half and slightly syrupy, then strain out the spices.
Serve the pears warm or chilled, standing upright in shallow bowls with the syrup spooned over. They keep in their syrup in the fridge for up to 3 days.

ingredientsStructured.name: lemon
ingredientsStructured.note: zest pared into strips and juiced

recipes.title: Rice pudding
ingredients: 4 tbsp strawberry jam, to serve, optional
steps: Put the rice, milk, sugar and butter in a heavy-based saucepan and bring slowly to a gentle simmer, stirring often.
Turn the heat down low and cook for 35–45 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the rice does not stick to the bottom of the pan.
The pudding is ready when the rice is completely soft and the milk has thickened to a creamy, spoonable consistency. Add a splash more milk if it gets too thick.
Stir in the vanilla and nutmeg, then serve warm with a spoonful of jam if you like.
Cool any leftovers within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 24 hours; reheat with a splash of milk until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Shortbread
ingredients: 100 g caster sugar, plus extra for sprinkling
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C). Grease and line a 20 cm square baking tin with baking paper.
In a mixing bowl, beat the butter and sugar together until smooth and pale.
Add the flour, cornflour and salt and work everything together with a wooden spoon, then your hands, until it just comes together into a smooth dough. Do not overwork it.
Press the dough evenly into the tin, smooth the top and prick all over with a fork. Mark into 16 pieces with a knife.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until pale golden all over and firm at the edges.
Sprinkle with a little caster sugar while hot, re-cut along the marks, then leave to cool completely in the tin before lifting out. Store in an airtight tin for up to a week.

recipes.title: Sticky toffee pudding
ingredients: 75 g unsalted butter, softened, for the sponge
75 g unsalted butter, for the sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C) and grease a 20 cm square baking dish.
Put the dates in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water, stir in the bicarbonate of soda and leave to soak for 10 minutes.

In a mixing bowl, beat the softened butter and light muscovado sugar until creamy, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, then stir in the dates with their soaking liquid and the vanilla to make a loose batter.
Pour into the dish and bake for 30–35 minutes until risen, firm to the touch and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.

Meanwhile, make the sauce: put the butter for the sauce, dark muscovado sugar and cream in a saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened.

Prick the warm pudding all over with a skewer, pour over a third of the sauce and leave for a few minutes to soak in. Cut into squares and serve with the remaining sauce. Refrigerate leftovers and reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Victoria sponge
ingredients: 1 tsp icing sugar, for dusting, optional
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (fan 170°C). Grease two 20 cm round sandwich tins and line the bases with baking paper.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the butter and caster sugar until very pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and fold in with the milk until smooth. Divide evenly between the tins and level the tops.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden, springy to the touch and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and leave to cool completely.

Whip the cream until it just holds soft peaks. Spread the jam over one sponge, top with the cream and sandwich with the second sponge. Dust with icing sugar if you like. Keep in the fridge because of the cream and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Apple slices with peanut butter dip
steps: In a mixing bowl, whisk the peanut butter, yogurt, honey and cinnamon together until smooth. Spoon into a small serving bowl.
Using a sharp knife, quarter and core the apples, then cut each quarter into thin slices.
Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice to stop them browning.
Arrange the slices around the dip and serve straight away.
Honey isn't suitable for babies under one year old, and this dip contains peanuts, so check for allergies before serving.

recipes.title: Baba ganoush
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C). Prick the aubergines all over with a fork and put them on a baking tray.
Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning halfway, until the skins are wrinkled and charred and the flesh has completely collapsed.
Leave until cool enough to handle, then halve and scoop the soft flesh into a sieve. Let it drain for 10 minutes to remove excess liquid.
Chop the flesh finely with a knife, or pulse briefly in a food processor, and tip into a mixing bowl.
Stir in the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, half the olive oil, the cumin and salt. Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed.
Spoon into a serving bowl, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and scatter with parsley and paprika, if using. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Cheese straws
ingredients: 75 g vegetarian mature cheddar, finely grated
25 g vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Unroll the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface and brush all over with beaten egg.
Mix the cheddar, hard cheese and paprika and scatter evenly over one half of the pastry. Fold the other half over the top and press down firmly with a rolling pin.
Brush the top with more egg, then use a sharp knife to cut the pastry into strips about 1 cm wide. Twist each strip a few times and lay on the baking tray.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until puffed, crisp and deep golden.
Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before serving. Keep leftovers in an airtight tin for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Courgette fritters
ingredients: 100 g Greek yogurt, to serve, optional
steps: Toss the grated courgettes with the salt in a sieve and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can with your hands or a clean tea towel.
Beat the eggs in a mixing bowl, then stir in the courgette, flour, feta, spring onions and pepper to make a thick batter.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Drop heaped tablespoons of the mixture into the pan, flatten slightly and cook for 3 minutes on each side until golden and set all the way through, with no runny egg in the centre.
Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper and repeat with the rest of the mixture, adding more oil as needed.
Serve warm with Greek yogurt for dipping, if you like.

recipes.title: Crispy roasted chickpeas
ingredients: 480 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Tip the chickpeas onto a clean tea towel and rub them dry, removing any loose skins.
Spread the chickpeas on a large baking tray, drizzle with the olive oil and shake the tray to coat them evenly.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway through, until deep golden and crunchy all the way through.
Meanwhile, mix the smoked paprika, cumin, garlic granules and salt in a small bowl.
Toss the hot chickpeas with the spice mix on the tray and leave to cool completely; they crisp up more as they cool.

Whole crunchy chickpeas are a choking hazard for children under five, so offer this snack to older children and adults only. Store in an open container and eat within 2 days, as they soften once sealed.

recipes.title: Cucumber and cream cheese bites
steps: Using a sharp knife, trim the ends of the cucumber and cut it into slices about 1.5 cm thick.
Use a teaspoon to scoop a shallow hollow from the centre of each slice, leaving a base so the filling doesn't fall through.
In a mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese with most of the dill, the lemon zest, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spoon or pipe a little of the cream cheese mixture into each cucumber slice.
Scatter with the remaining dill and serve straight away, or chill for up to 2 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Date and nut energy balls
steps: Put the cashews and almonds into a food processor and blitz until finely ground, with no large pieces left.
Add the dates, cocoa powder, vanilla extract and salt and blitz again until the mixture clumps together into a sticky dough. If it seems dry, add a teaspoon of water.
With damp hands, roll the mixture into 12 walnut-sized balls.
Tip the desiccated coconut onto a plate and roll each ball in it to coat.
Chill the balls on a plate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes to firm up.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week. These contain nuts, so check for allergies before sharing.

recipes.title: Devilled eggs
steps: Put the eggs into a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Simmer for 10 minutes so the yolks are fully set.
Drain the eggs and plunge them into a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes, then peel.
Using a sharp knife, halve the eggs lengthways and pop the yolks into a mixing bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the yolk mixture back into the egg whites and dust with paprika. Scatter over the chives, if using.
Serve straight away or keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Edamame with sea salt and chilli
ingredients: 400 g frozen edamame beans in pods
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil.
Add the frozen edamame and cook for 4–5 minutes until the beans inside the pods are tender.
Drain well in a colander and tip into a serving bowl.
Toss with the sesame oil, sea salt and chilli flakes while still hot.
Serve warm with lime wedges, if using, and an empty bowl for the pods. Squeeze the beans out of the pods with your teeth and discard the pods.

recipes.title: Frozen yogurt berry bark
ingredients: 200 g mixed fresh berries, larger berries halved
steps: Line a large baking tray with baking paper, making sure it fits flat in your freezer.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, honey and vanilla extract.
Spread the yogurt over the lined tray in an even layer about 1 cm thick.
Scatter the berries over the top, pressing them in lightly, then sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds, if using.
Freeze for at least 3 hours until completely firm, then break or cut into pieces with a knife.
Serve straight from the freezer, as it softens quickly. Store in a freezer bag for up to a month. Honey isn't suitable for babies under one year old.

recipes.title: Guacamole with baked tortilla chips
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Brush the corn tortillas lightly with the olive oil, stack them and cut each into 8 wedges with a sharp knife.
Spread the wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray and sprinkle with half the salt.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until crisp and lightly golden at the edges. They will crisp up further as they cool.
Meanwhile, halve and stone the avocados, scoop the flesh into a mixing bowl and mash with a fork, leaving a little texture.
Stir in the lime juice, red onion, tomato, fresh coriander and the remaining salt. Taste and add more lime if needed.
Serve the guacamole straight away with the cooled tortilla chips. If making ahead, press cling film onto the surface of the guacamole to stop it browning.

recipes.title: Hummus with vegetable sticks
ingredients: 240 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Put the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, ground cumin and salt into a food processor or blender.
Blend for a minute, then scrape down the sides. With the motor running, add the olive oil and cold water a spoonful at a time until the hummus is smooth and creamy.
Taste and add a little more lemon juice or salt if needed, then spoon into a serving bowl and dust with paprika, if using.
Using a sharp knife, cut the carrots, cucumber, red pepper and celery into sticks roughly the length of your finger.
Arrange the vegetable sticks around the hummus and serve. Keep leftover hummus covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Kale chips
ingredients: 200 g curly kale, tough stalks removed
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C (fan 130°C) and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Tear the kale into bite-sized pieces, wash and dry it very thoroughly; any water left on the leaves will stop them crisping.
Put the kale into a large mixing bowl, add the olive oil and massage it into the leaves with your hands until every piece is lightly coated.
Spread the kale in a single layer over the trays and sprinkle with the smoked paprika and salt.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until crisp but still green. Check often near the end as they can scorch quickly.
Leave to cool on the trays for a few minutes to crisp up fully, then serve the same day.

recipes.title: Seeded crackers
steps: In a mixing bowl, stir together all the seeds and the salt. Pour over the olive oil and boiling water, stir well and leave for 15 minutes until the chia and linseeds have thickened the mixture into a sticky paste.
Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Spread the mixture over the paper as thinly and evenly as you can, about 3 mm thick, using the back of a wet spoon. Leave no holes.
Bake for 30 minutes, then take out and use a knife to score into crackers. Carefully flip the whole sheet over.
Return to the oven for 20–25 minutes more until dry, crisp and golden at the edges.
Turn off the oven and leave the crackers inside to cool, then snap along the score lines. Store in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Spiced roasted nuts
ingredients: 1 sprig fresh rosemary, leaves finely chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (fan 150°C) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the olive oil, maple syrup, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne and rosemary.
Add the nuts and toss until evenly coated, then spread them in a single layer on the tray.
Roast for 12–15 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and fragrant. Watch closely towards the end as nuts burn quickly.
Sprinkle with the sea salt and leave to cool completely on the tray; they crisp as they cool.
Store in an airtight jar for up to a week. Whole nuts are a choking hazard for children under five, so don't give them to young children, and check for nut allergies.

recipes.title: Stovetop popcorn
steps: Put the sunflower oil and three popcorn kernels into a large saucepan with a lid and set over medium-high heat.
When the test kernels pop, add the rest of the kernels, shake the pan to coat them in oil and cover with the lid.
Cook, shaking the pan every few seconds, until the popping slows to a gap of about two seconds between pops, around 2–3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and leave the lid on for 30 seconds in case of late pops, then tip the popcorn into a large bowl.
Sprinkle with the salt and toss well, discarding any unpopped kernels. Popcorn is a choking hazard for children under five, so don't give it to young children.

recipes.title: Sweet potato wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C).
Using a sharp knife, cut the sweet potatoes in half lengthways, then cut each half into 3 or 4 even wedges, leaving the skin on.
Put the wedges on a large baking tray, add the olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic granules, salt and pepper and toss with your hands to coat.
Spread the wedges out in a single layer, skin-side down, leaving space between them so they roast rather than steam.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender in the middle and caramelised at the edges.
Leave to cool for a few minutes before serving, as the centres stay very hot.

recipes.title: Fresh tomato salsa
ingredients: 1 green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
steps: Using a sharp knife, quarter the tomatoes, scoop out the watery seeds and cut the flesh into small dice.
Put the tomatoes, red onion and green chilli into a mixing bowl.
Add the lime juice, coriander, olive oil and salt and stir gently to combine.
Leave to stand for 10 minutes so the flavours mingle, then taste and adjust the salt or lime.
Serve with vegetable sticks or tortilla chips. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within a day.

recipes.title: Homemade trail mix
steps: Put the almonds, cashews, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds into a dry large frying pan over medium heat.
Toast for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly golden. Tip onto a plate and leave to cool completely.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled nuts and seeds with the raisins, dried cranberries and chocolate chips.
Divide into small portions or store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks.
Whole nuts are a choking hazard for children under five, so don't give this mix to young children, and check for nut allergies before sharing.

recipes.title: Tzatziki with pitta chips
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C).
Coarsely grate the cucumber, then squeeze it firmly in a clean tea towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the cucumber, Greek yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, mint, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and a pinch of the salt. Chill while you make the chips.
Use a sharp knife to cut each pitta into 8 triangles, splitting them open into single layers.
Spread the pitta pieces on a large baking tray, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and sprinkle with the oregano and remaining salt.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool for a few minutes, then serve with the tzatziki.

recipes.title: Mexican black bean soup
ingredients: 480 g canned black beans, drained and rinsed
1 ripe avocado, diced, to serve, optional
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and red pepper and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the black beans, chopped tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Blend about half the soup with a stick blender, leaving plenty of whole beans for texture.
Stir in the lime juice and salt, then taste and adjust. Serve topped with coriander and avocado, if using.
To batch cook, cool and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

recipes.title: Butternut squash soup
ingredients: 1 kg butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and chopped
4 tbsp coconut milk, to swirl, optional
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the squash and stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the squash is very tender when pierced with a knife.
Blend with a stick blender, or carefully in batches in a blender, until velvety smooth. Add a splash of water if it's too thick.
Season with the salt and pepper, reheat until steaming and serve with a swirl of coconut milk, if using.
To batch cook, cool and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat from thawed until piping hot, stirring well.

recipes.title: Carrot and coriander soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and ground coriander and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrots, potato and stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Add most of the fresh coriander and blend with a stick blender, or in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Season with the salt and pepper, reheat until steaming and serve topped with the remaining coriander.
This soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

recipes.title: Chicken noodle soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook gently for 8 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken stock, add the thyme and bring to a simmer. Lower in the whole chicken thighs, then wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, the thickest part reaches 74°C and the juices run clear.
Lift the chicken onto a board and shred it with two forks. Remove the thyme stalks from the pot.
Bring the soup back to the boil, add the noodles and cook for 3–4 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming hot. Serve scattered with parsley, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the noodles for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, reheat until piping hot and cook fresh noodles in it.

recipes.title: French onion soup
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and stir to coat.

Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until starting to soften, then add the sugar, turn the heat to low and cook for 35–40 minutes more, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are soft, sticky and deep golden brown.
Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then sprinkle over the flour and stir for another minute.

Gradually pour in the stock, stirring and scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pot. Add the thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the herbs and season with the salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, heat the grill to high. Grill the baguette slices on a baking tray for 1–2 minutes each side until crisp, then top with the Gruyère and grill until bubbling.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and float two cheesy baguette slices on top of each to serve.
To batch cook, freeze the soup without the bread and cheese for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot and make the cheesy topping fresh.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup
ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, peeled and diced
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the leeks and onion, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft but not browned.
Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, then add the potatoes and stock.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, or leave some texture if you prefer.
Stir in the milk, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming without boiling. Serve scattered with chives, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the milk for up to 3 months. Potato soups can thicken on freezing, so thin with a little milk or water when reheating until piping hot.

recipes.title: Minestrone
ingredients: 240 g canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
100 g kale or savoy cabbage, shredded
1 tbsp fresh basil leaves, torn, optional
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, courgette and oregano and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cannellini beans and pasta and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender.
Add the kale or cabbage for the last 3 minutes until wilted. Season with the salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with basil, if using.

To batch cook, freeze the soup without the pasta for up to 3 months, then reheat until steaming hot and cook the pasta in it. Leftovers with pasta keep in the fridge for 2 days but the pasta will soften.

recipes.title: Creamy mushroom soup
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the mushrooms and thyme and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and are golden. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Scoop out a ladleful of mushrooms and set aside. Blend the rest with a stick blender until smooth, then return the reserved mushrooms for texture.
Stir in the double cream, season with the salt and pepper and heat until steaming without boiling. Serve scattered with parsley, if using.
To batch cook, freeze the soup before adding the cream for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot, then stir in the cream.

recipes.title: Pea and mint soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Add the potato and garlic, pour in the stock and bring to the boil. Simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the frozen peas and simmer for 3–4 minutes until just tender and still bright green.
Take off the heat, add the mint leaves and blend with a stick blender, or in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice, salt and pepper, and reheat gently if needed. Serve straight away to keep the colour fresh.
This soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Tomato and basil soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8–10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, stock and sugar. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrot is completely tender.
Take off the heat, add most of the basil leaves and blend with a stick blender, or carefully in batches in a blender, until smooth.
Season with the salt and pepper and reheat until steaming. Serve topped with the remaining basil.
This soup freezes well: cool, then freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.
